## 6. Direct evaluator, independent checks and scope

`two_below_all_positive.py` selects the branch, evaluates only the
fixed bounded constants, and returns (ER.14), or the already proved
T-046 count for \(k\ge5\). With `--polytopes` it exports all
constraint matrices in (ER.15). It calls no representation library,
elimination routine or input-dependent coefficient oracle.
Its continuation and branch checks passed 1960 comparisons,
including both determinant parities, and its 49 literal polytope
checks verified every one of 51 witnesses. The receipt is
`TWO_BELOW_ALL_EVALUATOR_CHECK.json`.

The rectangular agent independently checked all 791 valid
\(k=2,3,4\) coefficients through \(n\le6\), for every outer
label, by the cycle-index/Murnaghan–Nakayama calculation on the
actual plethysm side and literal fixed-pair induction on the
proposed side. All passed; the receipt is
`work/rectangular/OUTER5_TWO_BELOW_ENDPOINTS_CHECK.tsv`.
The complete proof above has been read and checked independently
by the rectangular and archive agents. The archive agent also
independently reconstructed all 1,520,400 constants using ambient
three-by-three Jacobi–Trudi characters, actual point jets, literal
fixed-pair induction and successive quotient-index differences.
All 56 per-branch/per-label hashes, extrema, active sets and the
eighteen endpoint exceptions agree; its receipt is
`work/archive/TWO_BELOW_ENDPOINTS_INDEPENDENT_RECEIPT.json`.
The whole-proof readings and the finite reconstructions are
recorded as distinct check events.

The primary inputs are the exact Cauchy and Young-projector maps,
the G-027 restriction complex and T-049 product-ideal comparison,
and the fully specified signed tensor Schur complex in the archive
appendix. Their source locators and complete proofs are retained in
those reports. The new work is the exact degeneration of the
restriction complex to (ER.8), the actual endpoint cohomology map,
the eight exhaustive positive branches, and the complete support
extension. No historical novelty claim is made.


# The complete three-below family, including triple intersections

## T-051. Positive formulas for every possible power

Let \(k\ge2\), \(x,b,d\ge0\), and \(2b+x+k\ge9\). Put
\[
n=d+b+x+k-3,\qquad
\lambda=(d+3b+2x+3k-12,d+b+x+2k-3,d+b+x,d+x,d).
\tag{ET.1}
\]
Every coefficient \(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\), \(\mu\vdash5\),
has the explicit positive formula in §4. It uses at most 55 bounded
integer polytopes of at most ten variables after selecting its
branch and residues. The new endpoints \(2\le k\le7\) use at
most seventeen polytopes of eight variables, or four of five
variables on branches with fixed \(b\).

The proof evaluates the entire exact arrangement restriction
complex. Three small endpoint sectors have a nonzero triple term;
their actual representations and quotient maps are retained rather
than omitted. The positive formula for \(k\ge8\) is T-048.
No historical novelty claim is made.

## 1. Actual jet comparison and the exact pair-to-triple sequence

Write \(a=b+x\), \(c=2k-3\), and
\(\alpha=(a+c,b+c,c)\). Then
\[
|\alpha|=2b+x+6k-9\ge5k.
\tag{ET.2}
\]
G-027 therefore gives its exact degree-\(|\alpha|\) restriction
complex. The determinant shift is
\[
S_\alpha Q=(\det E)^c\mathcal O(c)S_{(a,b)}Q
=\operatorname{sgn}_5\,\mathcal O(c)S_{(a,b)}Q,
\tag{ET.3}
\]
since \(c\) is odd. Also \(c\ge k-1\). The explicit
triangular jet-surjection proof in T-050 §1 consequently applies:
multiply scalar degree-\(c\) sections with arbitrary leading jets
through order \(k-1\) by global sections generating
\(S_{(a,b)}Q\), and prescribe the homogeneous jet layers in
order. Hence the singleton quotient in the arrangement complex is
the entire point-jet module, by the natural restriction map.

Since \(S_\alpha Q\) is acyclic in positive degrees, the same
cokernel comparison as (ER.8) gives the actual exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal I^k(c)S_{(a,b)}Q)
\longrightarrow K_2\longrightarrow K_3\longrightarrow0,
\qquad H^{q\ge2}(\mathcal I^k(c)S_{(a,b)}Q)=0.
\tag{ET.4}
\]
Here \(K_s\) is the \(s\)-subset term of G-027, including its
orientation, and then tensored by \(\operatorname{sgn}_5\)
to undo (ET.3). The map \(K_2\to K_3\) is the signed
polynomial quotient map of that complex followed by the specified
Schur-component identifications. This defines every map in (ET.4).

The balanced flag map still has the original sign
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbf Q^5)_{(n^5)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}
H^0(\mathcal I^k(c)S_{(a,b)}Q).
\tag{ET.5}
\]
Indeed \(\lambda_2=d+a+c\), and the sign from (ET.3) cancels
its odd \(c\). The chart inverse and normal-order comparison
are the actual ones of G-027, with \(\lambda_2-n=k\).

## 2. The pair term in every power

For a pair, put \(P=\mathbf Q^2\), with the endpoint permutation
action, and \(W=\mathfrak h_3\) for its complement. The exact
pair module, after the sign in (ET.3), is
\[
\begin{split}
K_2\simeq\operatorname{Ind}_{S_2\times S_3}^{S_5}\bigl(
&\det P\otimes P\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\\
&\oplus\det P\otimes W^*\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\\
&\oplus S_{(a-1,b)}W\oplus S_{(a,b-1)}W\bigr).
\end{split}
\tag{ET.6}
\]
The third summand is omitted at \(x=0\), and the fourth at
\(b=0\). This is the already evaluated four-summand module of
T-047 at defect three, now obtained directly for every \(k\ge2\).

Here is the complete two-slot calculation establishing (ET.6).
The truncated slots have total degree at most \(2k-2=c+1\).
The complementary Cauchy partition has at most two rows, so those
slots must supply the third row of length \(c\). There are only
two degrees to examine.

At degree \(c\), the slot degrees are
\((k-1,k-2)\) or \((k-2,k-1)\). Multiplication onto
\(\operatorname{Sym}^cF\) and the determinant polynomial map
used in (ER.7) identify their contribution with
\(P\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\) after orientation and (ET.3).
The standard intertwiner
\[
v_1e_1+v_2e_2\longmapsto
(e_1\wedge e_2)\otimes(v_1e_2-v_2e_1)
\tag{ET.7}
\]
identifies this with \(\det P\otimes P\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\).

At degree \(c+1\), both slots have degree \(k-1\). Only the
two Schur types \((c+1)\) and \((c,1)\) can contribute.
Their slot-exchange signs are respectively plus and minus: their
highest polynomials are
\(u_1^{k-1}v_1^{k-1}\) and
\((u_1v_2-u_2v_1)u_1^{k-2}v_1^{k-2}\).
Remove one further box from either of the first two rows of
\(\alpha\). If \(x>0\), removing the end of its first row
leaves a skew row of length \(c\) and one box in a different
column, so both types occur once. If \(b>0\), the same holds
when removing the end of its second row. If \(b=0\), that
second-row box shares the last column of the third row, so only
\((c,1)\) occurs. At \(x=0\), first-row removal is not a
partition and contributes nothing. These are all cases.

The maps are the corresponding row symmetrizers and column
antisymmetrizers, fixed by the displayed highest coefficients,
followed by Cauchy extraction. Equivalently, use the explicit
rank-two dual Pieri decomposition of
\(W^*\otimes S_{(a,b)}W\). For \(b\ge1\), its summands
are \(S_{(a-1,b)}W\) when \(x>0\), and
\(S_{(a,b-1)}W\). At \(b=0\), its second summand is the
actual rational representation
\((\det W)^{-1}\operatorname{Sym}^{a+1}W\), and its first
is present precisely when \(a>0\). The multiplication and
determinant highest-vector maps for this rank-two decomposition
are those fully proved in T-047. Keeping this second summand at
\(b=0\), and using the two slot-exchange signs just computed,
gives exactly the last three terms of (ET.6). This proves the
formula also at \(x=0\), \(b=0\) and \(k=2\).

## 3. Every triple term and its exact action

For three selected slots, the complementary standard space is the
one-dimensional sign representation of \(S_2\). A complementary
Cauchy partition has one row. The truncated factor must therefore
supply at least
\(\alpha_2+\alpha_3=b+4k-6\) boxes, and can supply at most
\(3(k-1)\). Thus
\[
K_3=0\qquad\text{whenever }b+k\ge4.
\tag{ET.8}
\]
The remaining possibilities are precisely \((k,b)=(3,0),(2,1)\)
and \((2,0)\). In the following formulas the second subgroup is
the two-letter complement:
\[
\boxed{
K_3=\begin{cases}
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_3\times S_2}^{S_5}
(\operatorname{sgn}_3\otimes\operatorname{sgn}_2^x),&(k,b)=(3,0),\\
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_3\times S_2}^{S_5}
([2,1]\otimes\operatorname{sgn}_2^{x+1}),&(k,b)=(2,1),\\
\operatorname{Ind}_{S_3\times S_2}^{S_5}
(([2,1]\oplus\operatorname{sgn}_3)\otimes
 (\mathbf1\oplus\operatorname{sgn}_2)),&(k,b)=(2,0).
\end{cases}}
\tag{ET.9}
\]

For \((3,0)\), the only normal degree is six: each slot has
degree two and the required normal Schur type is \((3,3)\).
Its multiplicity is one. Indeed, among the shapes in
\(S_{(2)}F\otimes S_{(2)}F\), only \((3,1)\) can acquire
a horizontal two-strip to give \((3,3)\). Its actual highest
vector in three slot rows is the product of brackets
\([uv][uw][vw]\), using the first two column coordinates.
It has degree two in each row and changes by the sign of a row
permutation. The complementary row has degree \(x+3\).
The \(S_3\) orientation and the \(S_3\) part of (ET.3)
cancel; the complementary sign becomes
\((-1)^{x+3+1}=(-1)^x\). This proves the first line of
(ET.9), with its concrete highest-vector map.

For \((2,1)\), every selected slot has degree one. The lower
two rows of \(\alpha=(x+2,2,1)\) force the normal Schur
type \((2,1)\), whose multiplicity in \(F^{\otimes3}\)
is the literal Specht module \([2,1]\) under the Young
projector. The complementary row has degree \(x+2\), giving
the sign \((-1)^{x+3}\) after (ET.3). The two \(S_3\)
signs again cancel, proving the second line.

For \((2,0)\), normal degrees two and three both occur.
At degree two, choose two nonempty slots and extract
\(\Lambda^2F\). Their action is
\(\operatorname{Ind}_{S_2}^{S_3}\operatorname{sgn}_2
=[2,1]\oplus\operatorname{sgn}_3\), and the complementary
row has degree \(x+1\). At degree three, the skew diagram
\((x+1,1,1)/(x)\) has Schur types \((2,1)\) and
\((1,1,1)\), each once; the actual maps are their Young
symmetrizer projections on \(F^{\otimes3}\). The same
two multiplicity modules occur, while the complementary row has
degree \(x\). Validity here gives \(x\ge7\), so neither
skew-diagram boundary is exceptional. After orientation and (ET.3),
the two complementary signs are \((-1)^x\) and
\((-1)^{x+1}\). Their sum is the fixed two-letter permutation
module, proving the last line of (ET.9).

These arguments define the triple identifications by polynomial
highest vectors and the specified rational Young projectors.
The map in (ET.4) remains the actual signed quotient map, not an
unspecified map between equal-dimensional representations.

In the fixed seven-class order, the triple traces are respectively
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q^{30}(x)&=(10,-3+(-1)^x,-2(-1)^x,1,(-1)^x,0,0),\\
Q^{21}(x)&=(20,2(-1)^{x+1},0,-1,(-1)^x,0,0),\\
Q^{20}&=(60,-6,0,0,0,0,0).
\end{aligned}
\tag{ET.10}
\]
They can be checked directly by summing fixed two-letter
complements: a fixed pair of letters or a two-cycle, with the
literal sign or standard character on the remaining three letters.

## 4. Complete positive endpoint certificates

Let \(P_g(x,b,k;c)\) be the explicit three-term Euler expression
(ER.9), with \(c=2k-3\). Let \(J_g^{(3)}(x,b)\) be the
four-summand pair traces (F.6)–(F.7), and let \(Q_g(x,b,k)\)
be (ET.10) on its three sectors and zero elsewhere. Exactness of
(ET.4) proves the actual zeroth-cohomology trace
\[
P_g(x,b,k;2k-3)+J_g^{(3)}(x,b)-Q_g(x,b,k).
\tag{ET.11}
\]
The scalar degree \(c-2=-1\) at \(k=2\) is handled by the
acyclic line bundle \(\mathcal O(-1)\) and the already fixed
zero convention for \(h_g(-1)\). No value is extrapolated past
an unproved initial range.

T-048 proves a positive formula for every \(k\ge8\). For each
\(k\in\{2,3,4,5,6,7\}\), set
\[
R_k=9-k,\qquad B_k=\lceil R_k/2\rceil.
\tag{ET.12}
\]
Use one branch \(b=B+B_k,x=X\), \(X,B\ge0\), and for
each \(0\le b_0<B_k\) use the branch
\(b=b_0,x=X+R_k-2b_0\), \(X\ge0\). These six
two-variable branches and fifteen one-variable branches are
disjoint and cover every valid endpoint. The three nonzero
corrections (ET.10) occur only in the indicated fixed-\(b\)
branches.

Pair (ET.11) with each fixed \(S_5\) character row. On a
two-variable branch, every residue function modulo 60 has separate
degrees at most \((3,4)\) and total degree at most five; its
active orders are the seventeen pairs (ER.11). On a one-variable
branch its degree is at most three. These statements are verified
by exact symbolic identities in the certificate: the identity
Euler trace is
\[
\frac{(x+1)(b+x+2)(b+1)}{12}
\bigl[(c+1)(b+c+2)(b+x+c+3)-5k(k+1)(k+2)\bigr],
\qquad c=2k-3.
\]
Add the pair dimension
\(60(x+1)\) for \(b>0\) or \(50x+40\) for \(b=0\),
and subtract the triple dimension 10, 20 or 60 on the three sectors. After each
shift in (ET.12), all its ordinary coefficients are positive.
The nonidentity degree bounds are three, three and one on the
transposition, double-transposition and three-cycle classes;
the remaining classes are periodic. All negative arguments are
\(-1\) or \(-2\), where the fixed residue expressions equal
zero exactly.

Define the bounded constants by the finite difference (ER.13),
now using the actual trace (ET.11) and the 21 branches (ET.12).
`three_below_endpoints_certificate.py` verifies all 3,049,200
integers. Every constant is nonnegative; every positive active
order is strictly positive, with minimum 941. The maximum
constant is 5668963200, and the largest proved signed-64-bit
intermediate bound is 5188937807741952. Exact symbolic degree
checks, all hashes, extrema and zero residues are saved in
`THREE_BELOW_ENDPOINTS_SUMMARY.json`.

For \(\nu=\mu\) or \(\mu^t\) according as \(d+b+x\) is
even or odd, the positive formula is
\[
\boxed{p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=\sum_{i\in\mathcal A_B}D_{\nu,B,r;i}
\prod_j\binom{q_j}{i_j},\qquad Z=r+60q.}
\tag{ET.13}
\]
Here \(Z\) is the free vector in its selected branch,
\(\mathcal A_B\) is (ER.11) or \(\{0,1,2,3\}\), and
\(D\) is the finite difference just defined. Newton's polynomial
identity proves equality for all parameter values, and the fixed
exhaustive certificate proves positivity. The complete literal
polytope matrices are (ER.15), with these parameters and constants.
The coefficient interval and increasing-chain bijection is
unchanged, proving the stated eight- or five-variable bounds.
Use T-048's already proved count for \(k\ge8\).

All first-order constants are positive, so the endpoint zero sets
are confined to their residue boxes. There are exactly 38 new
effective-label exceptions, retained as actual \((k,x,b)\)
triples in the fixed summary and obtained from its zero residues
by (ET.12). Together with T-048's seven valid exceptions, these
give a complete finite support decision for the whole family.
The evaluator performs precisely that branch and parity conversion.

## 5. Direct evaluator and proof status

`three_below_all_positive.py` computes (ET.13) using bounded
closed arithmetic constants and exports the complete integer
constraint matrices with `--polytopes`. It calls no representation
library, elimination routine or input-dependent multiplicity
oracle. Its direct continuation and branch checks passed 4312
comparisons, including both determinant parities. Its 147 literal
polytope checks verified all 398 witnesses. The receipt is
`THREE_BELOW_ALL_EVALUATOR_CHECK.json`.

The complete new proof has been read and checked independently by
the root, archive and rectangular agents. The rectangular agent independently
compared all 1561 valid \(2\le k\le7,n\le7\) coefficients,
for every outer label; 84 of those cases use an exceptional triple
module. Its comparison summed the literal cycle-stable three-subsets
and their restricted \(S_3\times S_2\) characters, rather than
calling (ET.10) or the endpoint evaluator. Every comparison passed;
the receipt is
`work/rectangular/OUTER5_THREE_BELOW_ENDPOINTS_CHECK.tsv`.
The archive agent independently reconstructed all 3,049,200 fixed
constants from the odd-sign-twisted ambient three-row Jacobi--Trudi
character, full point jets, literal fixed-pair induction and literal
fixed-triple induction. Its unbounded-integer successive-difference
calculation matched all 147 branch/label hashes, every active order
and extremum, and all 38 endpoint zeros. The independent receipt is
`work/archive/THREE_BELOW_ENDPOINTS_INDEPENDENT_RECEIPT.json`;
the complete proof review and reconstruction are recorded as A-056.
The source inputs
are G-027/T-049's exact arrangement construction, the signed tensor
Schur complex, and the explicitly proved Cauchy, Pieri and
rank-two maps in T-047. The added work is the all-power pair
calculation, all three actual triple modules, their quotient
sequence, the 21 positive endpoint branches and their direct
bounded-polytope implementation.


# A positive second-power formula and the complete first two ideal orders

## G-030. Zero twist at order two, with all boundary cases

Let \(x,b,d\ge0\), \(2b+x\ge10\), and put
\[
\begin{aligned}
n&=d+b+x-2,\\
\lambda&=(d+3b+2x-10,d+b+x,d+b+x,d+x,d).
\end{aligned}
\tag{ZS.1}
\]
Every \(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\), \(\mu\vdash5\), has the
positive formula (ZS.8). The branch \(b\ge5\) uses at most
seventeen bounded integer polytopes with eight variables after
selecting two residues. Each of the five branches \(0\le b\le4\)
uses at most four polytopes with five variables. The fixed constants,
complete support lists and direct constraint matrices are specified
below. This also completes every outer-five coefficient of ideal
order at most two, through the exact comparisons in §5.

## 1. Actual Schur extraction from the restriction complex

Write \(a=b+x\), \(E=\mathfrak h_5\), and let \(Q\) be the
rank-three tautological quotient on \(\mathbf P(E)\). The exact
balanced chart and exterior-column pairing of G021/TR3 give
\[
(S_\lambda\mathbf Q^5)_{(n^5)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}
H^0\bigl(\mathcal I_Z^2\otimes S_{(a,b)}Q\bigr).
\tag{ZS.2}
\]
The point order is \(\lambda_2-n=2\), and the line twist is
\(\lambda_2-\lambda_3=0\). The inverse chart is \(u^{-2}F(v(X))\),
with \(u=\prod_iX_{i1}\); G027's normal-order calculation proves
its polynomial extension precisely on the displayed ideal sections.

Use the rank-adaptive form of G027/T049 with auxiliary space
\(F=\mathbf Q^2\), \(\alpha=(a,b)\) and
\(N=a+b=2b+x\ge10\). The normal substitution and Cauchy
Young projector identify (ZS.2), before its sign, with
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}
\left(S_{(a,b)}F,\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^5
(\ell_i\otimes F)^2\right)_N\right).
\tag{ZS.3}
\]
The full exact restriction complex of G027 has, for a selected
subset \(A\) of size \(s\le3\), the quotient
\[
\left(\bigotimes_{i\in A}(\mathbf Q\oplus F)\right)
\otimes\operatorname{Sym}(\mathfrak h_{5-s}\otimes F),
\]
and the orientation line \(\bigwedge^s\mathbf Q^A\).
Its degree \(N\) terms for larger subsets vanish: their available
degree is at most four, below \(N\). The stabilizer splitting,
quotient maps and orientation are exactly FA13–17. Thus the
alternating Schur extraction computes an actual module through
specified polynomial maps.

Here is an explicit character of every term. For a permutation
cycle type \(\gamma\), let
\[
h_\gamma(j)=[z^j]\frac{1-z}{\prod_{\ell\in\gamma}(1-z^\ell)},
\qquad h_\gamma(j)=0\quad(j<0).
\]
For \(\rho=(p,q)\subseteq(a,b)\), set
\[
K_\gamma(a,b;p,q)=
h_\gamma(a-p)h_\gamma(b-q)
-h_\gamma(a-q+1)h_\gamma(b-p-1).
\tag{ZS.4}
\]
Use zero when \(\rho\) is not contained. This is precisely the
skew Schur trace \(s_{(a,b)/(p,q)}(\mathfrak h_{|\gamma|})\):
Macdonald, *Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials*, second
edition, Chapter I §5, (5.3)–(5.4), printed p.70, and
(5.7), p.71. The primary text and its derivation were read.
The multiplicity-space identification is Cauchy extraction
followed by the rational Young projectors, as in G027.

For selected cycle type \(\eta\), the cyclic tensor trace of its
truncated normal factors is
\[
P_\eta(X,Y)=\prod_{\ell\in\eta}(1+X^\ell+Y^\ell)
=\sum_{p\ge q\ge0}c_\eta(p,q)s_{(p,q)}(X,Y).
\tag{ZS.5}
\]
All the needed polynomials are the following finite table:

| \(\eta\) | Schur expansion \(P_\eta\) |
|---|---|
| empty | \(1\) |
| \((1)\) | \(1+s_1\) |
| \((1,1)\) | \(1+2s_1+s_2+s_{11}\) |
| \((2)\) | \(1+s_2-s_{11}\) |
| \((1,1,1)\) | \(1+3s_1+3s_2+3s_{11}+s_3+2s_{21}\) |
| \((2,1)\) | \(1+s_1+s_2-s_{11}+s_3\) |
| \((3)\) | \(1+s_3-s_{21}\) |

These identities follow by expanding the displayed products and
using \(s_{(p,q)}=\sum_{i=q}^pX^iY^{p+q-i}\).
In particular their coefficient is
\([X^pY^q]P_\eta-[X^{p+1}Y^{q-1}]P_\eta\), including
negative values when the first monomial is absent.

For \(g\in S_5\), its complete section trace is consequently
\[
t_g(x,b)=
\sum_{\substack{A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,5\}\\ |A|\le3,\ gA=A}}
(-1)^{\#\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}
\sum_{p\ge q}c_{\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}(p,q)
K_{\operatorname{cyc}(g|A^c)}(b+x,b;p,q).
\tag{ZS.6}
\]
The sign equals the restriction-complex sign
\((-1)^{|A|}\) times its actual orientation character
\((-1)^{|A|-\#\operatorname{cyc}(g|A)}\).
Character averaging gives
\(f_\nu(x,b)=120^{-1}\sum_{\text{classes }g}|g^{S_5}|
\chi_\nu(g)t_g(x,b)\).
The fixed seven character rows and sizes are those in T044.
The values are integral because the complex computes (ZS.3).

## 2. Exact residue-polynomial bounds

Every root in the generating series for \(h_\gamma\) has order
dividing60. Partial fractions make each nonnegative-index sequence
polynomial on residues modulo60. The empty-subset contribution is
the ordinary two-row Schur trace on \(E\). At the identity its
dimension is
\[
\frac{(x+1)(b+x+2)(b+x+3)(b+1)(b+2)}{12},
\]
of total degree five and separate degrees \((3,4)\).
At a transposition its unique eigenvalue of multiplicity three
has a quadratic contribution to \(h\); the degree-four products
cancel in its two-row determinant. All other eigenvalues have
multiplicity at most two. Thus every nonidentity term has total
degree at most three. These are the exact bounds proved in G026§2.

For a singleton subset, the complementary space has rank three.
Its identity complete traces are quadratic. The degree-four
terms in (ZS.4) agree and cancel, leaving degree at most three.
The degree in \(x\) is at most two. Each nonidentity complementary
class has maximum eigenvalue multiplicity two, so its products
have degree at most two. For a two-element subset the complement
has rank two; the identity products have degree two with equal
leading terms, and the other classes have bounded residue traces.
For a three-element subset the complement is a line, whose
nonnegative-index complete traces are periodic.

All normal partitions in the finite table have \(p\le3,q\le1\).
On the bulk \(b=B+5\), \(B\ge0\), every index in (ZS.4) is
nonnegative. Therefore the bounds just proved hold on every
entire bulk residue class, starting at zero: separate degrees at
most \((3,4)\), total degree at most five.

At a boundary \(0\le b\le4\), put
\(x=X+10-2b\). Then \(a=b+x\ge10-b\ge6\);
every varying index involving \(a\) is nonnegative. The indices
involving \(b\) alone are fixed constants, and negative ones
are assigned their exact zero values. The noncontainment tests
also involve only fixed \(b,q\). Thus each boundary residue
function is polynomial in \(X\) from \(X=0\), of degree at most
three. This checks every initial-range and partition-boundary issue.

## 3. Every fixed positive constant and its lattice polytope

In the bulk write \((x,B)=(r_1,r_2)+60(q_1,q_2)\), with
\(0\le r_i<60\), and define
\[
C_{\nu,r;i,j}=
\sum_{u=0}^i\sum_{v=0}^j
(-1)^{i+j-u-v}\binom iu\binom jv
f_\nu(r_1+60u,r_2+60v+5),
\quad0\le i\le3,\quad0\le j\le4.
\tag{ZS.7}
\]
The finite polynomial Newton identity gives
\[
\boxed{p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda=
\sum_{\substack{0\le i\le3,\ 0\le j\le4\\i+j\le5}}
C_{\nu,r;i,j}\binom{q_1}{i}\binom{q_2}{j},\qquad
\nu=\begin{cases}\mu&d+b+x\text{ even},\\
\mu^t&d+b+x\text{ odd}.\end{cases}}
\tag{ZS.8}
\]
The sign follows from (ZS.2), so no parity is implicit.

For \(b=0,1,2,3,4\), take the one-variable differences through

For each positive bulk constant, impose the integer constraints
\[
\begin{gathered}
60q_1=x-r_1,\quad60q_2=B-r_2,\quad q_1,q_2\ge0,\qquad
0\le y\le C_{\nu,r;i,j}-1,\\

Replacing each strict inequality by an integer gap of at least

selected tags, or240 fixed tags with all residues retained.
This proves the positive formula, including its complete matrices.

## 4. Complete support and direct evaluation

Both bulk first differences are strictly positive. A zero therefore
has \(q_1=q_2=0\), and the complete zero pairs in coordinates
\((x,B)=(x,b-5)\) are:

| \((5)\) | \((0,0),(0,2),(1,0)\) |
| \((4,1)\) | \((0,0)\) |
| \((3,2)\) | \((0,0)\) |
| \((3,1,1)\) | none |
| \((2,2,1)\) | \((0,0)\) |
| \((2,1,1,1)\) | \((0,0)\) |
| \((1^5)\) | \((0,0),(0,2),(1,0),(2,0)\) |

Every boundary first difference is positive, so its zeros have
\(0\le X<60\). The complete lists are:

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \((5)\) | 1 | 0,1 | none | 0 | none |

Use the effective label in (ZS.8) and the shift \(x=X+10-2b\).
All remaining inputs have positive coefficient, by nonnegativity
and the strict first-order bounds.

The evaluator second_power_zero_twist_positive.py computes only
the bounded constants (ZS.7) and bounded-order binomials at the
input. It exports the full integer matrices and lazily enumerates
witnesses, using the increasing-subset iterator already specified
in G023. The generic restriction-character implementation
zero_twist_arrangement.py was checked against1442 actual balanced
plethysm multiplicities at orders1,2,3; the separate fixed
certificate proves the infinite positive formula. Independent
constant, actual-character and literal-matrix checks are logged
with their precise executed scopes as they finish.

## 5. Completion of both first ideal orders and exact transport

For an arbitrary five-row partition of size \(5n\), set
\[
d=\lambda_5,\quad x=\lambda_4-\lambda_5,\quad
b=\lambda_3-\lambda_4,\quad
k=\max(0,\lambda_2-n),\quad c=\lambda_2-\lambda_3.
\tag{ZS.10}
\]
For positive \(k\), the exact flag dictionary is
\[
n=d+b+x+c-k,\qquad
\lambda=(d+3b+2x+4c-5k,d+b+x+c,d+b+x,d+x,d),
\]
with validity \(2b+x+3c\ge5k\). Its bundle is
\(\operatorname{sgn}^{d+b+x}\mathcal I^k(c)S_{(b+x,b)}Q\).
The following disjoint cases exhaust the first two ideal orders:

| Order | Twist | Complete positive formula |
|---|---|---|
| \(k=1\) | \(c=0\) | G026 |
| \(k=1\) | \(c=1\) | T045 |
| \(k=1\) | \(c\ge2\) | G021 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c=0\) | G030 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c=1\) | T051 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c=2\) | T050 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c=3\) | T045 |
| \(k=2\) | \(c\ge4\) | G021 |

Each row uses the actual chart (ZS.10); hence the coefficient,
parity and support comparisons agree exactly. At \(k=0\), G021
and its explicit \(u^{\,n-\lambda_2}\) stable chart in TR18
already give the complete positive count.

It follows that all seven coefficients are positively evaluated
for every five-row shape with
\[
\boxed{\lambda_2\le n+2\quad\text{or}\quad\lambda_4\ge n-2.}
\tag{ZS.11}
\]
For the second region use \(H=\lambda_1\),
\(\lambda^c=(H-\lambda_5,\ldots,H-\lambda_1)\),
\(n^c=H-n\). The exterior-column pairing TR19 identifies its
balanced module with the dual original module times
\(\operatorname{sgn}^H\), and
\(\lambda^c_2-n^c=n-\lambda_4\le2\). This is the exact
morphism proving the second region and its outer-label transpose.

The schemes are the affine and Proj coordinate models of the
five explicit linear ideals. G027's quotient substitution and
normal-order comparison, followed by its signed restriction
complex and Young projector, are the exact maps in (ZS.3).
EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2 (p.28) supplies the Proj charts and
II2.5.2,2.5.4 (p.31) the exact associated-sheaf functor.
The frame action is the comodule action of SGA3 I4.5,
I4.7.2–4.7.3. The Schur operations are SGA6
V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9 and cote133/024–029 via A010.
The finite equivariant free resolutions explicitly constructed
in G027§6 carry the coherent complex to locally free \(K_0\)
in SGA6 VI3.3. Thus its geometric class and every coefficient
use the same specified morphisms. R031 then gives the actual
symmetric canonical ranks on these evaluated components.


# Complete nonvanishing for outer degree five

## G-031. Every shape, every outer label and every inner degree

Let \(n\ge0\), \(\mu\vdash5\), and \(\lambda\vdash5n\).
The following fixed procedure decides exactly whether
\(p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda\) is positive. It uses a fixed table of344
integer vectors, the explicit strict-chamber rule G028, and a
bounded number of integer operations. No plethysm coefficient
remains to be evaluated by this decision procedure.

For length greater than five the coefficient is zero: the actual
Young projector embeds \(S_\mu(\operatorname{Sym}^n V)\)
in \((\operatorname{Sym}^n V)^{\otimes5}\), and repeated Pieri
allows at most five rows. Otherwise pad to five entries and put
\[
d=\lambda_5,\qquad g_i=\lambda_i-\lambda_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le4).
\tag{NW.1}
\]
Use the effective label \(\nu=\mu\) at even \(d\) and
\(\nu=\mu^t\) at odd \(d\).

For \(g=0\), the only nonzero effective label is \((5)\),
with multiplicity one. For all four gaps positive, G028 gives
the exact rule: the five middle labels always occur; both extreme
labels vanish on \(g=(L,1,1,1)\) and \(g=(1,1,1,L)\),
\(L\ge1\), \(L\equiv1\pmod5\); the effective trivial label
also vanishes at \(g=(1,2,2,1),(2,1,1,2)\). There are no
other strict-chamber zeros.

For every other gap vector use the following normal form. Write
\(g=(a,b,c,e)\), and first test the first line:
Set \(L_1=\max(1,3b+2c+e)\) and
\(L_4=\max(1,a+2b+3c)\). Then
\[
N(g)=
\begin{cases}
(L_1+(a-L_1)\bmod10,b,c,e),&a\ge L_1,\\
(a,b,c,L_4+(e-L_4)\bmod10),&e\ge L_4,\\
g,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\tag{NW.2}
\]
The first applicable line is used. The fixed catalog in §5
contains344 distinct vectors \(z\), each with its complete set
of zero effective labels. The exact decision is
\[
\boxed{\ p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda=0
\ \Longleftrightarrow\
N(g)\text{ is a catalog vector and }\nu
\text{ is one of its listed zero labels}.\ }
\tag{NW.3}
\]
This formula applies to the proper nonempty gap supports; the two
other cases were explicitly settled above. The supplied JSON and
TSV also give all seven exact multiplicities at every catalog
vector. They remain those values on its stable rays and on their
normal-form preimages.

This completes the full outer-five nonvanishing question. The
positive coefficient formulas already proved remain available in
their full stated regions. The present finding supplies a support
decision for every remaining coefficient, with all comparison maps
and a finite proof of exhaustion.

## 1. Exact stable maps in both end directions

Determinant multiplication gives the actual sign conversion in
(NW.1). Its normalized shape is
\[
\lambda^0=(a+b+c+e,b+c+e,c+e,e,0),\qquad
n_0=(a+2b+3c+4e)/5.
\tag{NW.4}
\]
The weighted sum is divisible by five. The first stable region
\(a\ge3b+2c+e\) is precisely \(\lambda^0_2\le n_0\).
The actual G027 quotient-section chart identifies its balanced
module with
\[
\operatorname{sgn}^{\,b+c+e}
S_{(b+c+e,b+c,b)}\mathfrak h_5.
\tag{NW.5}
\]
Increasing \(a\) by five multiplies the balanced expression
by \(u=\prod_iX_{i1}\); the shared full section space gives its
inverse on the image. Hence it is an isomorphism and preserves
every multiplicity.

For the second stable region use the perfect exterior-column
pairing in width \(H=a+b+c+e\). It identifies the balanced
module with the dual module of the reversed gap vector
\((e,c,b,a)\), times \(\operatorname{sgn}^H\).
The first stable inequality of that reversed vector is precisely
\(e\ge a+2b+3c\). Increasing \(e\) by ten increases \(H\)
by ten and the first gap of the complementary shape by ten.
Thus the same actual chart isomorphism and the unchanged
determinant sign preserve every multiplicity. A step of five in
this last direction instead transposes the effective label; using
ten in (NW.2) retains its complete vector.

The lower bound one in (NW.2) preserves the positive support
coordinate on a one-axis face. All subtractions are nonnegative
multiples of ten. They retain both the congruence and every zero
gap, and the maps just proved establish equality of all
coefficients before and after normalization.

Both stable inequalities can hold together only when \(b=c=0\)
and \(a=e\). At such a point each individual end direction has
its stated stable ray. These two rays must both be retained; their
interaction is explicitly checked below.

## 2. Every seed and every allowed increment

Fix a nonempty proper support \(S\subset\{1,2,3,4\}\).
For \(i\in S\), write
\(g_i=1+p_i+2t_i\), with \(p_i\in\{0,1\}\) and
\(t_i\ge0\); outside \(S\) put zero. Select a componentwise
minimal \(u\le t\) for which the weighted sum of
\((1+p_i)+2u_i\) is divisible by five.

Every such minimal \(u\) has total at most four. A list of five
indexed weights has two equal partial sums among its six partial
sums modulo five. It therefore contains a nonempty zero-sum
subvector, whose removal from a vector of total at least five
would contradict minimality. Enumeration of the finitely many
parities and \(u\) with total at most four gives all the seeds
used here. There are172 seeds across the fourteen supports.

The difference \(t-u\) belongs to
\[
M_S=\{v\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}^{S}:\ \sum_iiv_i\equiv0\pmod5\}.
\tag{NW.6}
\]
Every indecomposable nonzero element has total at most five:
a vector of greater total has a proper nonempty zero-sum
subvector of length at most five by the same partial-sum argument.
Thus enumerating total at most five and keeping the
componentwise minimal nonzero solutions gives the complete
generator list. Recursive subtraction proves generation.
Both these enumerations are literal fixed loops in
five_row_face_exploration.py, and all their outputs are retained.

For each generator \(h\), G024 gives an actual invariant-section
embedding from gap vector \(g\) to \(g+2h\), preserving
each outer label. To identify its highest weight explicitly,
put \(\eta_i=\sum_{j\ge i}h_j\), \(\eta_5=0\).
Then \(|\eta|=\sum_iih_i=5q\), so G024 multiplies by
the specified nonzero invariant section of weight \(2\eta\).
The tensor and chart degree increases are exactly the changes
in (NW.4). Every shape with all seven labels positive remains
fully positive after any later generator sequence.

## 3. Complete finite closure, including interacting rays

A catalog node is deficient: at least one of its seven
multiplicities is zero. Each node contributes its point. It
also contributes a ray \(z+10q\,e_j\), \(q\ge0\), for each
stable end axis \(j=1,4\) that it has. The union of these
points and rays will be denoted \(D_S\).

The algorithm starts from every deficient seed in support \(S\),
after normalization. For every retained node \(z\) and generator
\(h\), it evaluates \(N(z+2h)\). A fully positive value is an
exit. Every deficient value is retained and its transitions are
examined. In addition it makes the following finite checks for
each stable axis of every retained node.

Set \(w=z+2h\), and let
\[
L_1(w)=\max(1,3w_2+2w_3+w_4),\qquad
L_4(w)=\max(1,w_1+2w_2+3w_3).
\]
For the selected stable axis \(j\), put
\[
Q(z,h,j)=\max\left(0,\left\lceil
\frac{L_j(w)-w_j}{10}\right\rceil\right).
\tag{NW.7}
\]
The algorithm checks every \(q=0,\ldots,Q(z,h,j)\) in
\[
N(w+10q\,e_j).
\tag{NW.8}
\]
All are exits or retained deficient nodes.
Every generator has total at most five, and its largest
coefficient in either threshold is three. Since \(z\) was
already stable in direction \(j\), its threshold deficit
after adding \(2h\) is at most30. Hence \(Q\le3\).

For every \(q\ge Q\), \(w+10q e_j\) is stable in that same
axis. Its normal form is constant, because its other coordinates
are fixed and its varying coordinate has constant residue modulo
ten. At the possible equality of both stable inequalities,
\(w_2=w_3=0,w_1=w_4\), either normalization fixes the equality
point; the subsequent original-axis normalization has the same
value. This proves constancy also at that endpoint.
Thus (NW.8) exhausts the entire ray transition, including a
generator that raises its stability threshold or switches which
stable direction is selected. No commutation of normalization
with other increments is assumed.

The algorithm terminates with the following exact counts.
Support indices in this table refer to \(g_1,g_2,g_3,g_4\).
The ray-base count counts both directions at a node that has both.

| Support | Seeds | Nodes | Point transitions | Ray checks | Isolated points | Ray bases |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| 2 | 2 | 6 | 6 | 0 | 6 | 0 |
| 3 | 2 | 6 | 6 | 0 | 6 | 0 |
| 4 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| 1,2 | 8 | 52 | 208 | 160 | 32 | 20 |
| 1,3 | 8 | 16 | 64 | 56 | 8 | 8 |
| 1,4 | 6 | 30 | 90 | 160 | 0 | 40 |
| 2,3 | 6 | 10 | 30 | 0 | 10 | 0 |
| 2,4 | 8 | 16 | 64 | 56 | 8 | 8 |
| 3,4 | 8 | 52 | 208 | 160 | 32 | 20 |
| 1,2,3 | 30 | 24 | 192 | 192 | 12 | 12 |
| 1,2,4 | 30 | 52 | 416 | 552 | 16 | 36 |
| 1,3,4 | 30 | 52 | 416 | 552 | 16 | 36 |
| 2,3,4 | 30 | 24 | 192 | 192 | 12 | 12 |
| Total | 172 | 344 | 1896 | 2084 | 158 | 196 |

Here is the full exhaustion proof. Every input starts at one
of the proved seeds and is obtained by a finite generator
sequence. A fully positive seed or intermediate exit stays
positive, by the explicit multiplication injection. A deficient
seed belongs to \(D_S\), by normalization. For a point in
\(D_S\), the recorded point transition classifies its next
increment. For a ray point, (NW.7)–(NW.8) classify every next
increment, including its unbounded tail. A deficient target
normalizes to a retained node and hence belongs to its point
or stable ray. Induction along the finite generator sequence
proves that every deficient input belongs to \(D_S\).

Conversely every retained point has its computed deficient
vector; every ray has the same vector by the actual stable
isomorphisms. Thus every point of \(D_S\) is deficient.
Every retained node is already normalized, and normalizing
any of its ray points returns that node. Conversely (NW.2)
identifies every normal-form preimage with that node.
Consequently deficiency is exactly membership of \(N(g)\)
in the fixed node table. Its individual zero entries prove
(NW.3), including the determinant-label conversion.

## 4. Reproducible certificate, evaluator and geometric meaning

The complete source, normalized targets, raw targets, all seven
cycle traces and all seven multiplicities of every seed and
transition are in ALL_WALL_SUPPORT_GRAPH.json. The executable
all_wall_support_graph.py specifies every finite test just proved.
It checks all1896 point transitions and all2084 ray cases.
There are2218 distinct normalized evaluated gap vectors; the
largest normalized inner degree in those transitions is67.
These are finite character evaluations using the exact balanced
cycle-alternant/Pieri algorithm of G025, with the infinite input
range exhausted by the preceding proof.

ALL_WALL_SUPPORT_NODES.tsv gives every full vector in the344-node
catalog. FIVE_ROW_SUPPORT_INDEX.json is the fixed small evaluator
index, and five_row_support.py implements exactly (NW.1)–(NW.3)
and G028's strict rule. Its arithmetic count is fixed independently
of the input sizes; its integer bit cost is polynomial in their
bit lengths. It does no input-size representation computation.
The initial evaluator verification compared3640 actual support
entries on all congruent gap vectors in \(\{0,\ldots,5\}^4\),
including both determinant parities. Every exact exceptional
vector returned there also agreed. The independent reconstruction
and whole-proof reviews are recorded separately as they finish.

Every edge of this support proof is a specified invariant-section
map, and each normalization is the specified quotient-section
isomorphism or its perfect complementary-column pairing. The
frame action is SGA3 I4.5,I4.7.2–4.7.3; the Schur operations
are SGA6 V4.2,4.4,4.8–4.9 and cote133/024–029 via A010.
The frame and its five linear ideals have models over
\(\mathbf Z[1/5]\); in each fixed degree the rational Young
projectors are defined after additionally inverting the relevant
factorials. The rank statements here concern their characteristic-zero
generic fibers. This specifies the integral construction and its
scalar extension, without asserting equal ranks in every residue
characteristic.

EGA II2.4.1–2.4.2 gives the actual Proj charts, and
II2.5.2,2.5.4 the exact associated-sheaf functor. G027§6's
finite equivariant free resolutions carry the coherent complexes
to locally free \(K_0\) in SGA6 VI3.3. Thus the table decides
nonzero Schur-component ranks of those exact section modules.
For the symmetric canonical map, R031 then determines the actual
image rank by its source at \(n\le4\), its target minus the
eight stated kernel copies at \(n=5\), and its full target at
\(n\ge6\). These use the EGA I9.5.2 graded coordinate-image
scheme of that same normalized map.

# Charged oscillators, the frame quotient, and an exact theta branching realization

## T-052. The complete charge and lowest-type dictionary

Work over \(\mathbf Q\) for the polynomial maps, and extend scalars
to \(\mathbf C\) for the unitary groups. Let \(m\ge3\),
\(n\ge0\), \(\mu\vdash m\), and \(\lambda\vdash mn\)
with at most \(m\) parts. Pad \(\lambda\) by zeros. Define
\[
\begin{gathered}
e=\max(0,n-\lambda_2),\qquad n_0=n-e,\qquad
\lambda^0=(\lambda_1-me,\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_m),\\
r=m-2,\quad F=\mathbf Q^r,\quad W=\mathbf Q^m,
\quad k=\lambda_2-n_0,\\
\alpha=(\lambda_2-\lambda_m,\lambda_2-\lambda_{m-1},
\ldots,\lambda_2-\lambda_3),\quad N=|\alpha|,\quad
b=N-mk=\lambda^0_1-\lambda_2.
\end{gathered}
\tag{OC.1}
\]
All these are nonnegative integers, \(\lambda^0\) is a partition,
and \(|\lambda^0|=mn_0\). Let
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal P&=\mathbf Q[X_{ai},Y_i:1\le a\le r,1\le i\le m],\\
R_a&=\sum_iX_{ai}Y_i,\qquad C_a=\sum_i\partial_{X_{ai}}\partial_{Y_i},\\
Q_i&=\sum_aX_{ai}\partial_{X_{ai}}-Y_i\partial_{Y_i}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{OC.2}
\]
The superscript \([k]\) below imposes \(Q_i=k\) for every
\(i\). Subscripts \((N,b)\) impose the total \(X\)-degree
\(N\) and \(Y\)-degree \(b\). Put
\[
\mathcal H^{[k]}_{N,b}
=\mathcal P^{[k]}_{N,b}\cap\bigcap_{a=1}^r\ker C_a,
\qquad
K_{\alpha,k}=\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}
(S_\alpha F,\mathcal H^{[k]}_{N,b}).
\tag{OC.3}
\]
Here \(GL(F)\) acts on the \(X\) variables without a vacuum
twist. Column permutations act simultaneously on \(X_{ai}\)
and \(Y_i\). There is an actual rational \(S_m\)-module
isomorphism
\[
\boxed{(S_\lambda W)_{(n^m)}
\simeq\operatorname{sgn}^{\lambda_2}\otimes K_{\alpha,k}.}
\tag{OC.4}
\]
Its maps, including the dual comparison, are specified in §§3–5.
Consequently, writing \(\tau=\mu\) when \(\lambda_2\) is
even and \(\tau=\mu^t\) when it is odd,
\[
\boxed{p_{\mu,(n)}^\lambda
=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\tau],K_{\alpha,k}).}
\tag{OC.5}
\]

The same space is a lowest-type multiplicity for the actual unitary
dual pair \(U(r,1),U(m)\). More precisely, let \(L_k\) be the
one-column charged oscillator of §6. Then (OC.5) is the multiplicity
in \(S_\tau(L_k)\) of the irreducible lowest-weight oscillator
module whose lowest \(U(r)\times U(1)\) type has weights
\[
(\alpha_1+m/2,\ldots,\alpha_r+m/2;\,-b-m/2).
\tag{OC.6}
\]
All half-integral weights here refer to the stated metaplectic
preimages, or to a common covering group. The rational finite
identity (OC.4) uses ordinary permutation matrices after the
explicit vacuum untwist. No historical novelty is claimed for
the oscillator correspondence; the new comparison here assembles
it with T-049's actual diagonal quotient and the flag chart.

## 1. Every commuting operator and its scalar shift

Use indices \(a,b,c\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\), and add an index
\(0\). Define
\[
\begin{gathered}
A_{ab}=\sum_iX_{ai}\partial_{X_{bi}}+\frac m2\delta_{ab},
\qquad A_{00}=-\sum_iY_i\partial_{Y_i}-\frac m2,\\
A_{a0}=-R_a,\qquad A_{0a}=C_a,\\
B_{ij}=\sum_aX_{ai}\partial_{X_{aj}}-Y_j\partial_{Y_i}
       +\frac{r-1}{2}\delta_{ij},\qquad
G_{ij}=B_{ij}-\frac{r-1}{2}\delta_{ij}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{OC.7}
\]
They satisfy
\[
[A_{uv},A_{st}]=\delta_{vs}A_{ut}-\delta_{ut}A_{sv},
\quad [B_{ij},B_{pq}]=\delta_{jp}B_{iq}-\delta_{iq}B_{pj},
\quad [A_{uv},B_{ij}]=0.
\tag{OC.8}
\]
The \(G_{ij}\) are the ordinary algebraic \(\mathfrak{gl}(W)\)
action on \(\operatorname{Sym}(F\otimes W\oplus W^*)\).
In particular \(G_{ii}=Q_i\), whereas the oscillator's compact
diagonal weight on the charged space is
\((k+(r-1)/2)^m\).

Here is a direct verification of the signs and constants. The
polynomial Weyl relations give
\[
\begin{split}
[C_a,R_b]
&=\sum_iX_{bi}\partial_{X_{ai}}
  +\delta_{ab}\left(\sum_iY_i\partial_{Y_i}+m\right)\\
&=A_{ba}-\delta_{ab}A_{00},\\
[A_{ab},R_c]&=\delta_{bc}R_a,
\qquad [A_{ab},C_c]=-\delta_{ac}C_b,\\
[A_{00},R_a]&=-R_a,
\qquad [A_{00},C_a]=C_a.
\end{split}
\tag{OC.9}
\]
These identities, \([R_a,R_b]=[C_a,C_b]=0\), and the usual
matrix-unit brackets for \(X\partial_X\) prove the first
identity in (OC.8). The two terms in \(G_{ij}\) each give a
\(\mathfrak{gl}_m\) representation. Their commutators with
\(R_a\) cancel as \(X_{ai}Y_j-X_{ai}Y_j\); their
commutators with \(C_a\) cancel as well. This proves every
mixed bracket. The centers agree literally:
\[
\sum_aA_{aa}+A_{00}=\sum_iB_{ii}
=N_X-N_Y+\frac{m(r-1)}2.
\tag{OC.10}
\]
Thus all \(A\)'s preserve each joint charge space.

Give monomials the Fischer inner product
\(\langle X^uY^v,X^{u'}Y^{v'}\rangle
=\delta_{u,u'}\delta_{v,v'}u!v!\). Then
\[
R_a^\dagger=C_a,\quad A_{ab}^\dagger=A_{ba},\quad
A_{00}^\dagger=A_{00},\quad
A_{a0}^\dagger=-A_{0a},\quad B_{ij}^\dagger=B_{ji}.
\tag{OC.11}
\]
For a matrix in \(\mathfrak u(r,1)\), the coefficients of
\(E_{a0}\) and \(E_{0a}\) are complex conjugates; (OC.11)
makes its action skew-adjoint. The compact
\(\mathfrak u(m)\) action is skew-adjoint by the last identity.
These are exactly the two real forms with the declared shifts.

## 2. The real symplectic embedding and the vacuum character

Let \(H=\mathbf C^{r,1}\), \(W=\mathbf C^m\) with their
Hermitian forms, conjugate-linear in the first entry. On the real
vector space underlying \(H\otimes W\), take
\(\omega=\operatorname{Im}(h_H\otimes h_W)\).
The tensor actions of \(U(r,1)\) and \(U(m)\) are mutual
centralizers in its real symplectic group.

Indeed, a real-linear map commuting with the first group commutes
with its scalar \(i\), so is complex-linear. Its complex
commutant is \(1_H\otimes\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf C}(W)\).
One can see this without a real-form assumption: diagonal phases
give the diagonal matrix units on \(H\), positive-coordinate
unitaries give the matrix units within the positive block, and a
boost between a positive and the negative coordinate gives the
remaining off-diagonal units. Preservation of \(\omega\),
together with complex linearity, implies preservation of the
Hermitian form, since
\(\operatorname{Re}h(v,w)=\omega(v,iw)\). The commutant
inside the symplectic group is therefore exactly \(U(m)\).
The reverse argument starts with the natural irreducible \(U(m)\)
action and yields \(U(r,1)\).

Choose the positive compatible complex structure equal to \(i\)
on the positive part and \(-i\) on the negative part. Its
holomorphic creation space is
\(F\otimes W\oplus W^*\). For
\((a,z,g)\in U(r)\times U(1)\times U(m)\), its action is
\(a\otimes g\) on \(X\) and \(z^{-1}g^{-t}\) on
\(Y\). With the positive-energy oscillator convention of T-001,
the polynomial Fock space is tensored with the vacuum character
\(\chi_0\) on the metaplectic preimage, where
\[
\chi_0^2=(\det a)^m z^{-m}(\det g)^{r-1}.
\tag{OC.12}
\]
The half derivative of this determinant is exactly the collection
of constants in (OC.7). Thus (OC.7) is the actual oscillator
restriction for this real dual pair.

The \(GL(F)\) action used in (OC.3) removes the
\((\det a)^{m/2}\) vacuum factor. The ordinary column action
\(G\) removes the compact vacuum character \(\chi_W\),
whose square is \((\det g)^{r-1}\). If \(r\) is odd,
the explicit section of this cover with
\(\chi_W(g)=(\det g)^{(r-1)/2}\) gives the finite factor
\(\operatorname{sgn}^{(r-1)/2}\) on permutation matrices.
If \(r\) is even, retain the pullback double cover and its
character \(\chi_W\), then tensor by \(\chi_W^{-1}\).
This cancels the central kernel and descends to the literal
\(S_m\) action. In particular no fractional power of the sign
character is being used as a character of \(S_m\).

The primary oscillator source used here is Basile–Joung–Mkrtchyan–
Mojaza, *Dual Pair Correspondence in Physics: Oscillator Realizations
and Representations*, arXiv:2006.07102v2, §5.2, equations
(5.21)–(5.30), printed pp.29–31, at
[the primary PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.07102).
Its parameters are \(M_+=r,M_-=1,N=m\). Equations
(5.21)–(5.22) give these operators and shifts; (5.27)–(5.30)
give the traceless lowest types. The complete cited passages were
read, including the dual tensor construction (A.25)–(A.28).
The source's double-cover convention is explicit in (1.16),
printed p.7, and its oscillator monodromy calculation is
(2.12)–(2.18), printed p.10.

## 3. The actual charge homogenization and quotient map

Put
\[
D_k=\bigotimes_{i=1}^m\operatorname{Sym}^{\ge k}F
\subset\mathbf Q[Z_{ai}],\qquad L_a=\sum_i Z_{ai}.
\tag{OC.13}
\]
On a polynomial \(f\) homogeneous of degree \(d_i\ge k\)
in each block, define
\[
\Phi_k(f)=f(X)\prod_iY_i^{d_i-k}.
\tag{OC.14}
\]
This is a rational \(GL(F)\times S_m\)-equivariant bijection
from \(D_k\) to \(\mathcal P^{[k]}\). Its inverse erases
the \(Y\)'s: a charge-\(k\) monomial has forced exponent
\(d_i-k\) on \(Y_i\). It preserves \(X\)-degree and
satisfies
\[
\Phi_k(Z_{ai}f)=X_{ai}Y_i\Phi_k(f),
\qquad \Phi_k(L_af)=R_a\Phi_k(f).
\tag{OC.15}
\]
For \(E=\mathfrak h_m\), write
\(I_i=(\ell_i\otimes F)\subset\operatorname{Sym}(E\otimes F)\)
with \(\ell_i=e_i-\mathbf1/m\). The complete all-degree
theorem T-049, including its actual substitution map, gives
\[
J_k=\bigcap_i I_i^k=\prod_iI_i^k
\simeq D_k/(L_1,\ldots,L_r)D_k.
\tag{OC.16}
\]
Therefore for \(b=N-mk\ge0\), (OC.14) induces
\[
(J_k)_N\simeq
\mathcal P^{[k]}_{N,b}\big/
\sum_aR_a\mathcal P^{[k]}_{N-1,b-1}.
\tag{OC.17}
\]
A space with negative degree is zero. Each arrow in (OC.17)
is induced by (OC.14) and the literal substitution
\(Z_{ai}\mapsto\ell_i\otimes f_a\).

The Fischer orthogonal complement of the denominator is exactly
\(\mathcal H^{[k]}_{N,b}\), by \(R_a^\dagger=C_a\).
Both the denominator and this kernel are stable under
\(GL(F)\times S_m\). Thus orthogonal projection gives an
equivariant isomorphism of the quotient with that kernel.
It is also rational and completely finite. On the indicated
finite-dimensional space set \(T=\sum_aR_aC_a\), and factor
its rational characteristic polynomial as
\(\det(t-T)=t^s q(t)\), \(q(0)\ne0\). Then
\[
\pi_{\mathrm{harm}}=q(T)/q(0).
\tag{OC.18}
\]
The operator \(T\) is positive semidefinite and self-adjoint;
its kernel is the common kernel of the \(C_a\)'s. It is
diagonalizable, so (OC.18) is one on its zero eigenspace and zero
on every other eigenspace. This includes an invertible \(T\),
when the result is zero, and \(T=0\), when it is the identity.
The zero-dimensional case has its unique zero map. The inverse
of the resulting map is inclusion of a harmonic vector followed
by the quotient in (OC.17).

For clarity, (OC.14) also transports lowering to the explicit
operator
\[
\Phi_k^{-1}C_a\Phi_k
=\sum_i(N_i-k+1)\partial_{Z_{ai}},
\qquad N_i=\sum_aZ_{ai}\partial_{Z_{ai}}.
\tag{OC.19}
\]
The rightmost derivative acts first; on block degree \(d_i\)
the coefficient is \(d_i-k\). At \(d_i=k\) it is zero,
so it preserves the truncated space. The induced monomial norm
is \(\prod_i u_i!(d_i-k)!\). With this norm (OC.19) is
the adjoint of multiplication by \(L_a\). This independently
checks the endpoint and every scalar in the charge map.

## 4. The finite harmonic member of theta correspondence

Let \(V_\gamma(W)\) denote the irreducible rational
\(GL(W)\)-module of highest weight \(\gamma\). The
traceless tensor form of the compact-member correspondence is
\[
\mathcal H_{N,b}
\simeq
\bigoplus_{\substack{\alpha\vdash N\\\ell(\alpha)\le r}}
S_\alpha F\otimes
V_{(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r,0,-b)}(W).
\tag{OC.20}
\]
Here \(\mathcal H_{N,b}\) imposes the lowering equations but
does not yet impose charge. This is the specialization
\(M_-=1\) of the source's (5.27)–(5.30). Its exact tensor
map is polarization into \(F\)-slots and \(W\)-slots,
application of their Young idempotents, and contraction of a
\(W\) slot with a \(W^*\) slot. The equations \(C_a=0\)
say precisely that all such contractions vanish after the
\(F\)-Young projection. The source's Levi–Civita map
(A.25) turns each covector column into its complementary vector
column; its relation (A.27) is the resulting Young relation.
It identifies the surviving irreducible highest weight in
(OC.20). Our lengths satisfy \(\ell(\alpha)+1\le m-1\)
when \(b>0\), so this use is strictly within that tensor range.

There is also a useful normalization of every displayed embedding.
Let \(\Delta_j=\det(X_{ai})_{1\le a,i\le j}\), and
\(\alpha_{r+1}=0\). Send the product of the standard highest
vectors in (OC.20) to
\[
v_{\alpha,b}=Y_m^b\prod_{j=1}^r
\Delta_j^{\alpha_j-\alpha_{j+1}}.
\tag{OC.21}
\]
It is nonzero, has \(GL(F)\)-weight \(\alpha\) and
ordinary \(GL(W)\)-weight \((\alpha,0,-b)\), and is
annihilated by every \(C_a\): its \(Y\) derivative uses
column \(m\), while its \(X\)'s use columns at most \(r\).
The compact raising operators kill the first-column minors.
Applying the two enveloping-algebra actions to (OC.21) supplies
the unique normalized intertwiner in (OC.20). This describes
the actual summand map as well as its labels. In the oscillator
action the compact weight in (OC.20) is shifted by
\((r-1)/2\) in every coordinate, and its lowest noncompact
type is (OC.6), directly from (OC.7).

Taking the charge weight in (OC.20) gives an ordinary
\(S_m\)-module isomorphism
\[
K_{\alpha,k}\simeq
\left(V_{(\alpha,0,-b)}(W)\right)_{(k^m)}.
\tag{OC.22}
\]
It uses literal permutation matrices for the \(G\) action.
The full compact group preserves the harmonic space; its
equal-weight subspace is preserved by these permutations.

## 5. Every determinant, dual, and first-row map in (OC.4)

First suppose \(e=0\). A direct calculation from (OC.1) gives
\[
\gamma=(\alpha,0,-b)
=\lambda_2\mathbf1-(\lambda^0_m,\ldots,\lambda^0_1).
\tag{OC.23}
\]
The actual rational representation map is
\[
V_\gamma(W)\simeq
(\det W)^{\lambda_2}\otimes(S_{\lambda^0}W)^*.
\tag{OC.24}
\]
To fix it without suppressing the dual, put
\(H=\lambda^0_1=\lambda_2+b\) and
\(\beta=(H-\lambda_m^0,\ldots,H-\lambda_1^0)
=(\alpha_1+b,\ldots,\alpha_r+b,b,0)\).
Columnwise exterior multiplication in the \(m\)-by-\(H\)
rectangle, followed by the Schur projections, is the perfect pairing
\[
S_{\lambda^0}W\otimes S_\beta W
\longrightarrow(\det W)^H.
\tag{OC.25}
\]
It is nonzero on complementary highest and lowest column tensors;
the highest weights are contragredient with this determinant
twist, so the induced pairing is perfect. Tensoring its second
factor by \((\det W)^{-b}\) gives (OC.24), with its
normalization matched to (OC.21). This also works when \(b=0\).

On the charge weight, (OC.24) reads
\[
K_{\alpha,k}\simeq
\operatorname{sgn}^{\lambda_2}\otimes
\left((S_{\lambda^0}W)_{(n_0^m)}\right)^*,
\tag{OC.26}
\]
since \(k-\lambda_2=-n_0\). The sign is exactly the
determinant of the permutation matrix in (OC.25).

We now give the dual comparison actually used in (OC.4). Realize
\(S_{\lambda^0}W\) as the image of a rational Young
idempotent in \(W^{\otimes mn_0}\). Equip the standard rational
basis of \(W\) with its dot product and use the tensor product
form. Restriction to this image, and then to its balanced weight
space, is nondegenerate: after extension to \(\mathbf R\)
the form is positive definite. Permutation matrices preserve it
and commute with the Young idempotent. Hence
\[
v\longmapsto\bigl(w\longmapsto\langle v,w\rangle\bigr)
\tag{OC.27}
\]
is a rational \(S_m\)-equivariant isomorphism to that balanced
space's dual. This map concerns the specified finite group action;
no \(GL(W)\)-self-duality is being substituted for (OC.24).

Finally allow \(e>0\). In T-032's flag algebra let \(x_i\)
be the first-column variables and \(u=\prod_i x_i\). The
balanced chart gives the actual bijection
\[
\cdot u^e:
(S_{\lambda^0}W)_{(n_0^m)}
\longrightarrow (S_\lambda W)_{(n^m)}.
\tag{OC.28}
\]
Indeed its right highest weight increases by \((me,0,\ldots,0)\),
its left weight increases by \((e^m)\), and both sides are
the same tail flag module in that chart. The inverse divides
by \(u^e\), with polynomiality proved in T-032 by the exact
minor count. Also \(u\) is fixed by every slot permutation.
When \(n>\lambda_2\),
\(\lambda^0_1=\lambda_2+N\ge\lambda_2\), so all its
partition and degree conditions hold. Composing (OC.28),
(OC.27), (OC.26) and (OC.22) proves (OC.4). Combining this
with T-003's balanced-weight Schur–Weyl map proves (OC.5).
The empty partition at \(n=0\) gives \(k=N=b=0\) and a
single trivial harmonic vector, so it is included.

There is a second explicit route through the frame ideal:
T-032/G-027's flag map and relative Schur pairing identify the
balanced module with
\(\operatorname{sgn}^{\lambda_2}
\operatorname{Hom}_{GL(F)}(S_\alpha F,(J_k)_N)\).
Equations (OC.14)–(OC.18) identify this with (OC.4).
Thus the charged oscillator and the frame-ideal model are related
by the actual homogenization, quotient and harmonic projection,
in addition to their compact highest-weight comparison.

## 6. A Schur functor of one charged lowest-weight module

For one column, the same homogenization identifies the charge-\(k\)
space with
\(L_k=\bigoplus_{d\ge k}\operatorname{Sym}^dF\).
Write \(z_a\) for its variables and \(N_z\) for their degree.
The \(\mathfrak{gl}_{r+1}\) action is
\[
\begin{gathered}
A^{(1)}_{ab}=z_a\partial_{z_b}+\tfrac12\delta_{ab},
\quad A^{(1)}_{00}=-N_z+k-\tfrac12,\\
A^{(1)}_{a0}=-z_a,
\qquad A^{(1)}_{0a}=(N_z-k+1)\partial_{z_a}.
\end{gathered}
\tag{OC.29}
\]
The last operator acts by \((d-k)\partial_{z_a}\) in
degree \(d\). Its lowest compact type is
\(\operatorname{Sym}^kF\otimes(\det F)^{1/2}\)
with negative \(U(1)\) weight \(-1/2\).

This algebraic lowest-weight module is irreducible. A nonzero
submodule contains a nonzero homogeneous element: the degree
operator is diagonal and a polynomial in it isolates any of the
finitely many degree components of a vector. Choose the least
degree occurring in the submodule. At degree \(d>k\) some
derivative is nonzero, and (OC.29) lowers that degree, a
contradiction. At degree \(k\) the irreducible compact
\(\operatorname{Sym}^k F\) is therefore present. Multiplication
by the \(z_a\)'s generates every higher symmetric power, so
the submodule is all of \(L_k\). The transported Fischer form
supplies its unitary oscillator realization on the corresponding
cover. This argument also covers \(k=0\).

Tensoring (OC.29) over the \(m\) columns gives exactly
(OC.7) on \(\mathcal P^{[k]}\), by (OC.14). Thus
\[
L_k^{\otimes m}\simeq\mathcal P^{[k]}
\tag{OC.30}
\]
as an actual module for the noncompact oscillator algebra and
the literal tensor-permutation \(S_m\). All group statements
can be read on a common cover of \(U(r,1)\); the tensor
vacuum exponents sum to \(m/2\), as required by (OC.7).

The compact-member theta decomposition, with its summands generated
by (OC.21), gives
\[
S_\tau(L_k)\simeq
\bigoplus_{\substack{\alpha,b\ge0\\|\alpha|-b=mk}}
\mathcal D^{(m)}_{\alpha,b}\otimes
\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}
\left([\tau],(V_{(\alpha,0,-b)}W)_{(k^m)}\right).
\tag{OC.31}
\]
Here \(\ell(\alpha)\le r\), and
\(\mathcal D^{(m)}_{\alpha,b}\) is the irreducible oscillator
module with the lowest compact type (OC.6). The algebraic direct
sum in (OC.31) consists of finite polynomial vectors. The
displayed map is the known theta summand inclusion generated
from (OC.21), followed by taking the \(S_m\) Hom space in
(OC.30). Distinct labels have distinct lowest compact types.
Equations (OC.22), (OC.26) and (OC.27) therefore make its
specified multiplicity exactly (OC.5).

The irreducibility and direct sum in this application can also
be checked directly from (OC.20). In every finite total degree,
Fischer decomposition writes
\(\mathcal P_D=\mathcal H_D+\sum_aR_a\mathcal P_{D-2}\).
The \(R_a\)'s commute with the compact column action, so
iteration generates each column isotypic component from its
harmonics. For a given \(\gamma=(\alpha,0,-b)\),
(OC.20) gives exactly one harmonic bidegree and the irreducible
lowest \(GL(F)\) type \(S_\alpha F\). A nonzero submodule
of its column multiplicity space contains a homogeneous vector:
a polynomial in the energy
\(\sum_aA_{aa}-A_{00}=N_X+N_Y+m(r+1)/2\)
isolates a degree component. Its least occurring degree is killed
by every lowering operator. It therefore meets that unique
lowest type, contains the whole type by compact irreducibility,
and generates the full multiplicity space by the preceding
Fischer recursion. This proves irreducibility. The ordinary
isotypic direct sum for the compact group then gives (OC.31)
with the actual summand inclusions already specified.

The relevant lowest vectors can be obtained entirely in a finite
space: impose (OC.3), row degrees \(\alpha_a\), and
\(\sum_iX_{ai}\partial_{X_{bi}}=0\) for \(a<b\),
then apply the Specht Hom projector. All these rational operators
are explicit and commute with the slot action. The positive
lowest-type decomposition does not remove that last projector;
the general positive counts G-009–G-011 and the direct families
already proved evaluate it by their separately established maps.

## 7. Endpoints and proof status

At \(b=0\), every charged monomial has each block degree
exactly \(k\), so no lowering or quotient relation occurs:
\(\mathcal H^{[k]}_{mk,0}=(\operatorname{Sym}^kF)^{\otimes m}\).
Equation (OC.5) becomes the complementary-partition plethysm
identity with shape \(\alpha\), inner degree \(k\), and
the sign \(\operatorname{sgn}^{\lambda_2}\). Its actual
map is precisely the column pairing (OC.25). At \(k=0\),
(OC.16) is the polynomial quotient by the diagonal subspace,
\(J_0=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathfrak h_m\otimes F)\);
this recovers the stable flag chart through (OC.14)–(OC.18).
For \(\ell(\lambda)>m\), T-002's Cauchy decomposition
gives zero, and no oscillator label is needed.

The exact script `oscillator_charge_checks.py` verified 1895
normal-ordered Weyl-algebra commutator identities in ranks
\((r,m)=(1,3),(2,4),(3,5)\), together with the adjoints and
center identities. It constructed 42 literal rational joint
lowering/compact-raising nullspaces and their permutation traces.
After both determinant parities and the allowed first-row shifts,
all 663 plethysm coefficients and 663 class traces agreed with
the independent cycle-index/Murnaghan--Nakayama implementation.
Six exact characteristic-polynomial projectors passed idempotence,
lowering-kernel and rank checks. The largest tested polynomial
domain had dimension 200. The receipt is
`OSCILLATOR_CHARGE_RECEIPT.json`; these finite computations support
the all-parameter proofs and do not replace them.

The root, rectangular and archive agents independently read and checked the complete proof
(OC.1)–(OC.31), including the real centralizers, every scalar
shift, rational projection, actual dual form and first-row map,
and one-column irreducibility; all three whole-proof reviews passed.
The rectangular and archive agents also independently read the
full primary §5.2 and Appendix A passages and their cover
conventions. The direct isotypic-generation argument following
(OC.31) was independently supplied and checked by the archive
agent in its review. Its full review is recorded as A-061.


# The charged incidence algebra and the actual frame Rees algebra

## T-053. Multiplication, a quadratic degeneration, and its exact finite-group obstruction

Let \(m\ge3\), \(1\le r\le m-2\), \(F=\mathbf Q^r\),
and \(E=\mathfrak h_m\). Retain T-049's frame ideals
\(I_i=(\ell_i\otimes F)\) and
\(J_k=\bigcap_i I_i^k=(J_1)^k\subset
S=\operatorname{Sym}(E\otimes F)\). Define
\[
\mathcal P=\mathbf Q[X_{ai},Y_i],\qquad
R_a=\sum_{i=1}^m X_{ai}Y_i,\qquad
\mathcal B=\mathcal P/(R_1,\ldots,R_r).
\tag{IR.1}
\]
Give \(X_{ai}\) column charge \(e_i\), \(Y_i\) column
charge \(-e_i\), and give \(X_{ai}\) row weight
\(\varepsilon_a\), \(Y_i\) row weight zero. The relations
have charge zero and row weights \(\varepsilon_a\).
There is an actual \(GL(F)\times S_m\)-equivariant graded
algebra isomorphism
\[
\boxed{\mathcal R(J_1)=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}J_kt^k
\simeq\bigoplus_{k\ge0}\mathcal B_{(k^m)}.}
\tag{IR.2}
\]
The degree \(k\) on the right is the equal nonnegative charge;
polynomial degree in \(S\) corresponds to \(X\)-degree.
Every row-weight component has the explicit positive count in
(IR.8), using at most \(2^r\) bounded integer polytopes of
\(rm+m\) variables. These count the entire indicated torus
weight space. The highest-type and Specht projectors that give
individual plethysms remain the explicit ones of T-052.

In the displayed coordinates, no monomial initial ideal of
\((R_1,\ldots,R_r)\) is preserved by the literal column
permutation action of \(S_m\). The proof in §4 is a
degree-two orbit calculation for this specified action.

## 1. The algebra map and every grading

In \(\mathbf Q[Z_{ai}]\), put
\(D_k=\bigotimes_i\operatorname{Sym}^{\ge k}F\) and
\(L_a=\sum_i Z_{ai}\). On a polynomial with block degrees
\(d_i\ge k\), use the charge map of T-052,
\[
\Phi_k(f)=f(X)\prod_iY_i^{d_i-k}.
\tag{IR.3}
\]
It is linear on the direct sum of block-homogeneous pieces.
Since each \(R_a\) has charge zero,
\[
\mathcal B_{(k^m)}
=\mathcal P_{(k^m)}/\sum_aR_a\mathcal P_{(k^m)}.
\]
The equations \(\Phi_k(L_af)=R_a\Phi_k(f)\) therefore
give the component isomorphism
\(D_k/LD_k\simeq\mathcal B_{(k^m)}\).
T-049 identifies its left side with \(J_k\) by literal
substitution \(Z_{ai}\mapsto\ell_i\otimes f_a\).

For \(f\in D_k\) and \(g\in D_l\), first take them
block-homogeneous with degrees \(d_i\), \(d'_i\).
Then \(fg\in D_{k+l}\) and
\[
\Phi_k(f)\Phi_l(g)
=f(X)g(X)\prod_iY_i^{d_i+d'_i-k-l}
=\Phi_{k+l}(fg).
\tag{IR.4}
\]
Bilinearity proves the same identity for all \(f,g\).
The multiplication in \(D_k/LD_k\) maps to multiplication
of their substituted polynomials in \(J_k\). Hence (IR.4)
proves multiplication compatibility across every pair of degrees,
and proves (IR.2), including its unit at \(k=0\).

In particular the degree-zero coefficient algebra map sends
\(\ell_i\otimes f_a\) to \([X_{ai}Y_i]\); the relations
\(\sum_i\ell_i=0\) map to \(R_a=0\). A generating
degree-one element of the Rees algebra has the concrete image
\[
t\prod_{i=1}^m(\ell_i\otimes f_{a_i})
\longmapsto\prod_{i=1}^m X_{a_i i}.
\]
These formulas specify the algebra map on generators; their
well-definedness and bijectivity are exactly (IR.3)–(IR.4) and
the proved component quotient.

The maps preserve row weights, \(X\)-degree and slot
permutations. At equal charge \(k\), the \(Y\)-degree
is forced to be \(N-mk\) for \(X\)-degree \(N\).
The full \(GL(F)\) action is also preserved: the \(R_a\)'s
transform as \(F\), and both homogenization and substitution
commute with row changes of basis. Thus the torus gradings and
the larger equivariance have distinct, specified roles in (IR.2).

For a scheme description, let \(T=(\mathbf G_m)^m\) act
with the stated charges, and introduce a variable \(z\) of
charge \((-1,\ldots,-1)\). Then
\[
\mathcal R(J_1)\simeq(\mathcal B[z])^T,
\qquad f\in\mathcal B_{(k^m)}\longmapsto fz^k.
\tag{IR.5}
\]
Indeed an invariant polynomial has exactly these charge-homogeneous
terms, with \(k\ge0\) because its \(z\)-exponent is
nonnegative. Formula (IR.4) makes this identification an algebra
map. The inclusion of invariant rings defines the actual affine
quotient morphism from the incidence scheme \(XY=0\), with
this extra affine coordinate, to \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal R(J_1)\).
Slot permutations fix \(z\) and normalize \(T\), so this
morphism retains their action. T-049's explicit Rees charts and
relative Proj construction therefore apply to this same algebra.

## 2. A complete quadratic Gröbner calculation

Use a graded monomial order: compare total degree first, then
the weight assigning one to \(X_{aa}\), \(1\le a\le r\),
and zero to every other variable, then a fixed lexicographic
order. It gives
\[
\operatorname{in}(R_a)=X_{aa}Y_a,
\qquad
\operatorname{in}(R_1,\ldots,R_r)
=(X_{11}Y_1,\ldots,X_{rr}Y_r).
\tag{IR.6}
\]
Here is a direct normal-form proof of the second equality.
Write \(M_a=X_{aa}Y_a\) and
\(T_a=-\sum_{i\ne a}X_{ai}Y_i\), and replace every
factor \(M_a\) by \(T_a\). Each replacement strictly
decreases the total degree in the diagonal variables
\(X_{11},\ldots,X_{rr}\), since no \(T_a\) contains
any of these variables. Thus rewriting terminates. The leading
monomials are pairwise coprime. If two different rules apply to
a monomial \(qM_aM_b\), applying them in either order gives
\(qT_aT_b\). The case of two occurrences of the same rule
has the identical replacement. Induction on diagonal-variable
degree therefore proves that every sequence of reductions has
the same linear normal form: after either first rule, apply the
other, and use the induction hypothesis for every lower-degree
term. This argument extends linearly to polynomials.

The normal form kills every multiple of \(M_a-T_a=R_a\),
and every reduction preserves its residue modulo the relation
ideal. Hence the standard monomials give a basis of the quotient.
Moreover every rewriting step lowers the chosen monomial order.
A relation with a standard leading monomial could not reduce to
zero, since lower monomials never create that leading monomial.
This proves (IR.6), including the asserted Gröbner-basis property.
Every reduction preserves row weight, column charge and the two
degrees in \(X\) and \(Y\).

This also proves that \(R_1,\ldots,R_r\) is a regular
sequence, without a dimension inference. Suppose \(f\) is a
nonzero standard representative modulo the first \(a-1\)
relations. The leading monomial of \(R_af\) is
\(M_a\operatorname{in}(f)\). Since \(M_a\) uses no
variable in the previous leading monomials, that product is not
divisible by any of them. Thus \(R_af\) is nonzero modulo
the preceding relations. This is the required injectivity at
each step.

The degeneration itself is explicit. Set
\[
\mathscr B=\mathbf Q[s,X,Y]\big/
\left(X_{aa}Y_a+s\sum_{i\ne a}X_{ai}Y_i:1\le a\le r\right).
\tag{IR.7}
\]
The same proof works over \(\mathbf Q[s]\), replacing
\(M_a\) by \(sT_a\): the two possible reductions of
\(M_aM_b\) both give \(s^2T_aT_b\), and termination
uses the same diagonal-variable degree. The standard monomials
therefore form a free \(\mathbf Q[s]\)-basis. In particular
this is a flat family. Its fiber at \(s=0\) is the monomial
quotient in (IR.6), and its fiber at \(s=1\) is \(\mathcal B\).
Over \(s\ne0\), the map from (IR.7) to
\(\mathcal B[s,s^{-1}]\) sends its \(X_{aa}\) to
\(sX_{aa}\), and fixes all other \(X\)'s and \(Y\)'s;
the inverse sends the original \(X_{aa}\) to
\(s^{-1}X_{aa}\). It sends each relation to \(sR_a\).
These are the exact general-fiber isomorphisms.

Every row-weight and charge piece is free with its indicated
standard basis. Selecting the equal nonnegative charge pieces
therefore gives a flat algebra family whose general fiber is
the Rees algebra in (IR.2). These maps retain the stated torus
gradings; their behavior under the full permutation action is
settled separately in §4.

## 3. The literal bounded polytopes

Fix \(k\ge0\) and a row weight
\(\eta=(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r)\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}^r\).
For each \(A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}\), use integer
variables \(u_{ai}\) and \(v_i\), with constraints
\[
\begin{gathered}
u_{ai}\ge0,\quad v_i\ge0,\qquad
\sum_i u_{ai}=\eta_a,\qquad
\sum_a u_{ai}-v_i=k,\\
a\in A:\quad u_{aa}=0,\ v_a\ge1,\qquad
a\notin A:\quad v_a=0.
\end{gathered}
\tag{IR.8}
\]
Call this rational polytope \(\mathscr P_{A}(\eta,k)\).
It is bounded: each \(u_{ai}\le\eta_a\), and the column
equations give \(0\le v_i\le|\eta|\). Its point
\((u,v)\) gives the monomial \(X^uY^v\). The row and
charge equations give exactly the required weight, and the last
conditions guarantee that no \(X_{aa}Y_a\) divides it.
Conversely every standard monomial has the unique tag
\(A=\{a\le r:v_a>0\}\), and gives exactly one point of
(IR.8). Thus there is a proved bijection and
\[
\boxed{\dim(\mathcal B_{(k^m)})_\eta
=\dim(J_k)_\eta
=\sum_{A\subseteq[r]}
\#\bigl(\mathscr P_A(\eta,k)\cap\mathbf Z^{rm+m}\bigr).}
\tag{IR.9}
\]
If \(|\eta|<mk\), summing the column equations forces
\(\sum_i v_i<0\), so every polytope is empty. The zero
weight at \(k=0\) has its single point in the empty tag.

This also identifies precisely which representation-theoretic
sum the count evaluates. Put \(N=|\eta|\), \(b=N-mk\).
When \(b<0\), all the spaces and counts are zero by the
summed charge equation. For \(b\ge0\),
write \(K_{\alpha,k}\) for T-052's ordinary multiplicity
space for the current row dimension. When \(r<m-2\), pad
\(\alpha\) by zeros and add zero-degree \(X\) rows.
Inclusion of polynomials independent of those rows identifies
the highest multiplicity spaces literally: the new lowering
and compact raising equations vanish, and their zero row weights
force every polynomial in the enlarged space to be independent
of those rows. Thus this is the space of T-052 with the padded
partition. The actual \(GL(F)\times S_m\) decomposition gives
\[
\dim(J_k)_\eta
=\sum_{\substack{\alpha\vdash N\\\ell(\alpha)\le r}}
\dim(S_\alpha F)_\eta\;\dim K_{\alpha,k}
=\sum_{\alpha,\tau}
K_{\alpha,\eta}\,\dim[\tau]\,
\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\tau],K_{\alpha,k}).
\tag{IR.10}
\]
To specify every last factor, set
\[
\gamma=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r,0^{m-r-1},-b),
\quad t=\alpha_1,\quad n=t-k,\quad
\lambda=t\mathbf1-\operatorname{reverse}(\gamma).
\]
For a nonzero component, \(N\ge mk\), whence
\(t\ge N/r\ge k\). Thus \(n\ge0\), and
\(\lambda\) is a partition of \(mn\), with
\(\lambda_2=t\). The zero partition has \(t=k=n=0\).
The actual zero-row inclusion just given, followed by T-052's
column pairing and rational balanced dual map, yields
\[
\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{S_m}([\tau],K_{\alpha,k})
=p_{\tau^{(t)},(t-k)}^\lambda,
\qquad
\tau^{(t)}=\begin{cases}\tau&t\text{ even},\\
\tau'&t\text{ odd},\end{cases}
\]
where \(\tau'\) is the conjugate partition. The finite twist
is exactly \(\operatorname{sgn}^t\).
Equation (IR.10) therefore specifies both positive weights and
every plethysm label in the sum. The individual factors are
obtained by the highest-type and Specht maps in T-052;
(IR.9) counts their displayed weighted sum.

## 4. The narrowly stated permutation obstruction

Let \(\prec\) be any monomial order in the fixed coordinates
of (IR.1), and set \(I=(R_1,\ldots,R_r)\). Its degree-two
space is exactly the \(r\)-dimensional span of the \(R_a\)'s.
Consequently \(\operatorname{in}_\prec(I)_2\) is an
\(r\)-dimensional monomial space. Every one of its monomials
is \(X_{ai}Y_i\) for some \(a,i\): these are all the
monomials that occur in the degree-two relations. There are no
relations in smaller degree.

The column-permutation orbit of any such monomial is
\(\{X_{aj}Y_j:1\le j\le m\}\), a set of exactly
\(m\) distinct monomials. A permutation-stable monomial
space containing one must contain all of them. This would force
\(r\ge m\), contrary to \(r\le m-2\). Hence
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{in}_\prec(I)
\text{ is not stable under the literal }S_m
\text{ column action for any such monomial order}.}
\tag{IR.11}
\]
This disproves the particular proposal that standard monomials
from a monomial degeneration in these coordinates inherit that
same slot-permutation action. It makes no claim about a change
of coordinates, other equivariant filtrations, or the already
proved positive formulas. The original quotient and the Rees
algebra retain their actual \(S_m\) actions through (IR.2).

## 5. Exact resolution and Grothendieck transport

The regular sequence proved in §2 gives the actual finite
\(GL(F)\times GL(W)\)-equivariant free resolution
\[
0\longrightarrow\mathcal P\otimes\Lambda^rF
\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow
\mathcal P\otimes F\longrightarrow\mathcal P
\longrightarrow\mathcal B\longrightarrow0,
\tag{IR.12}
\]
where the \(j\)-th term is shifted by \((j,j)\) in
\((X,Y)\)-degree. The differential is
\[
f\otimes(f_{a_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge f_{a_j})
\longmapsto\sum_{h=1}^j(-1)^{h-1}R_{a_h}f
\otimes f_{a_1}\wedge\cdots\widehat{f_{a_h}}
\cdots\wedge f_{a_j}.
\tag{IR.13}
\]
Its charge is zero, \(GL(W)\) fixes each \(R_a\), and
\(GL(F)\) acts on their span as \(F\). These facts prove
equivariance of every differential. Selecting a torus weight is
exact because a rational torus representation is the direct sum
of its weight spaces. Thus each finite bidegree and equal-charge
piece gives, in the representation Grothendieck group of
\(GL(F)\times S_m\),
\[
[(J_k)_N]=[\mathcal H^{[k]}_{N,b}]
=\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^j
[\Lambda^jF\otimes\mathcal P^{[k]}_{N-j,b-j}].
\tag{IR.14}
\]
The first equality is the actual rational projection of T-052,
and the second is the Euler relation of (IR.12), rather than
an equality inferred from dimension. Under (IR.3), the cyclic
trace of its tensor factors is T-049's factored character.

On \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal P\), (IR.12) is a finite
equivariant vector-bundle resolution of the coherent module
defined by the closed incidence immersion. The action is given
by the polynomial coactions specified in (IR.1). Sheafifying
the graded resolution on \(\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal P\)
uses the exact graded sheafification map; T-049 §7 records its
verified EGA and SGA locators. The Rees identification (IR.2)
is a separate algebra isomorphism, so it also induces literal
isomorphisms on its affine scheme and relative Proj charts.
This states the base of each resolution and each geometric map.

## 6. Proof status

The full argument above proves every multiplication and grading,
the specified quadratic Gröbner basis, the flat-family maps,
the standard-monomial/polytope bijection, the degree-two
permutation obstruction and the exact equivariant resolution.
The standalone `charged_incidence_polytopes.py` exports all
integer matrices in (IR.8), and optionally enumerates their
standard monomials. Its reproduction script
`check_charged_incidence.py` passed 151 row-weight/charge cases,

`CHARGED_INCIDENCE_RECEIPT.json`.

The root and archive agents read the whole proof and passed its
