### The finite reduction and its actual transport

Write the four gaps as \(2+p_i+2t_i\), with \(p_i\in\{0,1\}\).
Choose a coordinate-minimal \(u\le t\) satisfying the stated
size congruence modulo five. Such a minimal vector has
\(\sum_i u_i\le4\): from any five residues among \(1,2,3,4\),
two of the six partial sums coincide, giving a nonempty
zero-sum submultiset. Subtracting it preserves the congruence
because two is invertible modulo five, contradicting
coordinate minimality. This proves the completeness of
the finite enumeration over sixteen parity vectors and
seventy vectors of total size at most four.

For the resulting minimal partition \(\sigma\), put
\(d=\lambda_5\) and
\(\eta=(\lambda-d\mathbf1-\sigma)/2\).
Its consecutive gaps are \(t_i-u_i\), so it is a partition.
Its size is a multiple of five, since
\(2|\eta|=5(n-d-n_\sigma)\).
Thus the exact injection (ER1), followed by determinant
multiplication, transports every seed multiplicity to
the desired component, with its precise sign twist.

### Independent sign and coefficient checks

The single-cycle alternant has exponents
\(e_i=\alpha_i+\ell-i\). Repeated residues modulo \(\ell\)
give zero. Distinct residues give the row-permutation
sign relative to ascending residues, multiplied by
\((-1)^{\ell(\ell-1)/2}\), the denominator's descending
order sign. Total degree \(\ell n\) then gives exactly
the power \(T^n\). Fixed-point removal is the actual
Pieri expansion by a horizontal \(n\)-strip, with
interlacing and total-size constraints. Its branching
formula has no extra cycle sign.

For two two-cycles, separating the even and odd exponents
in the four-row determinant gives the two two-variable
Schur factors in IN10. The permutation sign is
\((-1)^{N+3}\), where \(N\) counts odd-before-even pairs;
the denominator has three such pairs. The interval
coefficient formula therefore has the displayed sign
and endpoint constraints.

For a three-cycle and a two-cycle, Laplace expansion on
the first three columns has sign
\((-1)^{\sum_{i\in I}i+6}\), with one-based row indices.
The cross resultant is \(T_1^2-T_2^3\), with positive
leading term. Its Laurent expansion is
\[
(T_1^2-T_2^3)^{-1}
=\sum_{v\ge0}T_1^{-2v-2}T_2^{3v}.
\]
Consequently the numerator exponents satisfy
\(A=n+2v+2,\ B=n-3v\), exactly as in the report.
The ten row subsets give the claimed finite expression.
The program's zero-based exponent differs from the
one-based expression by an even integer, so the signs agree.

The independent program check_gap2_seeds_independent.py
does not use these alternant residue formulas. It
enumerates minimal congruence vectors independently,
uses interlacing strips, evaluates literal integer
Jacobi–Trudi determinants for single cycles, and uses

the two-cycle cases. The interpolated degree is at most
twenty-four. The actual two-two trace has absolute
value at most \(n+1\le13\), and the three-two trace
has absolute value at most ten. Centering the residue
therefore recovers the unique exact integer.

The execution compared all seventy-six seeds, all
532 class traces and all 532 multiplicities. It used

interpolations. Every result agrees; the smallest
multiplicity is two and the largest seed inner degree
is twelve. The separate degree-four source and target

GAP2_SEEDS_INDEPENDENT_RECEIPT.json.

### Exact degree-four grid-map calculation

The polynomial \(F_0\) in IN16 is a product of the stated

### Exact primary-source range and propagation

Cheung–Ikenmeyer–Mkrtchyan, Symmetrizing tableaux and the
5th case of the Foulkes conjecture, arXiv:1509.03944v1,
defines its map on printed p. 2 by symmetric-tensor
inclusion, transpose of the rectangular tensor grid,
and symmetric projection. This is the actual map used
in G025. Theorem 6(a), printed p. 3, proves injectivity
at \((5,6)\). Theorem 6(b), at the same location, lists
the eight kernel weights at \((5,5)\). Each of the
eight has a consecutive gap zero or one after padding
to five rows. Thus none lies in the present interior.
Both statements and the map definition were opened
and read. Their original large evaluation matrices
were not regenerated in this run.
Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.03944 .

Christian Ikenmeyer, On McKay's propagation theorem for
the Foulkes conjecture, arXiv:1509.04957, defines the
same grid map on printed p. 2. Theorem 1.3 is on that
page, and its complete proof is §§2–6, printed pp. 3–8.
All of this proof was read. The following precise
normalization clarifications make its auxiliary maps
literal without changing any kernel:

1. In tensor degree \(D=ab\), the source defines
   \(\phi_{ij}=D^{-1}\sum_p\zeta_{ij}^{(p)}\).
   Hence its two-operator coefficient is \(D^{-2}\),
   rather than the printed \(1/[D(D-1)]\). Terms with
   the same tensor position vanish, and the remaining
   double sum commutes term by term.
2. Removing the \(a\) fixed \(f_b\) positions in §4
   multiplies the lower raising product by exactly
   \(((b-1)/b)^{a(b-1)}\). This scalar is nonzero.
3. In §5, fixing positions of the other letters leaves
   their spectator factor tensored with
   \((\mathbf Q^2)^{\otimes(b+i-1)}\). The displayed
   \(GL_2\) computation applies on every copy. On the
   summand \(\det^{\eta_2}\operatorname{Sym}^{b+i-1-2\eta_2}\),
   the weight vector maps with coefficient
   \((b-\eta_2)/D\). Since
   \(\eta_2\le i-1<a<b\), it is nonzero.

One can also identify the source's raising map with
the normalized transversality map exactly. Index a
source basis by unordered partitions into \(a\)
blocks of size \(b\), and a target basis by unordered
partitions into \(b\) blocks of size \(a\); use averages
over the block labels. The raising-product entry is
\(b!/D^D\) precisely when every source-target block
intersection has size one, and zero otherwise.
Normalized group averaging has the same incidence
entry \(b!/(b!)^a\). The two maps differ by the explicit
nonzero scalar \((b!)^a/D^D\). Under the symmetric
tensor pairings this is the transpose-grid map on
the Schur multiplicity spaces. The propagation proof
therefore establishes injectivity of the actual
specified map at every \((5,n)\), \(n\ge6\).
Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1509.04957 .

The normalized symmetric-tensor projectors are
self-adjoint, so transposition gives surjectivity of

the interior types from the exact square kernel
gives the same componentwise conclusion. Rationality
and the actual inclusion into larger vector spaces

# Exact finite-normal audit of the stable defect formula

Statement **A-048**. Complete proof review of T047, performed on
21 November 2026 by GPT-6 Astra Pro, run /root/archive_audit;
effort setting not exposed.

**Result: complete proof PASS.** The entire report
work/theta/outer5/stable_defect_cohomology_report.md, D.1–D.17,
and both its evaluator and check program were read. The proof
establishes its actual higher-cohomology isomorphism for every
\(s\ge2,\ k\ge3s-1,\ a=b+x,\ b,x\ge0\), with \(c=2k-s\).
Its stated zeroth-cohomology consequence is the exact Euler
character plus the evaluated correction. This audit gives that
assertion its precise stated scope.

## 1. The directional interpolation maps

The four tangent directions at a frame point form a projective
frame in \(\mathbf P^2\). The two quadrics
\[
f=z_1z_2-z_1z_3,\qquad
g=z_1z_2-z_2z_3
\]
have exactly the four displayed projective zeros and independent
gradients there. Their complete intersection is reduced and has
length four. In particular they form a regular sequence.
For \(r=s-1\), the generators \(f^{r-i}g^i\) and the adjacent
relations \(g e_{i-1}-f e_i\) give the exact complex
\[
0\longrightarrow S(-2r-2)^r
\longrightarrow S(-2r)^{r+1}
\longrightarrow J^r\longrightarrow0.
\]
The proof by successive division modulo \(f\) checks every
syzygy. Injectivity on the left follows in order from the
coordinates, since \(f\) and \(g\) are nonzero divisors.
After sheafification and twist \(d\ge2r\), the left summands
have twist at least \(-2\). Projective-plane cohomology proves
that evaluation onto all order-\(r\) directional jets is
surjective. This is the literal polynomial-evaluation map.

The independent calculation also formed those matrices directly
in affine charts for the four direction points. For every
\(1\le r\le8\), their ranks at \(d=2r\) are the full
\(4\binom{r+1}{2}\) row ranks. At \(d=2r-1\), their ranks are
the full column ranks, giving the predicted failure to cover
all jets at that lower degree. Each rank is witnessed by a
maximal nonzero minor modulo \(1000003\), and therefore proves
the same maximal rank over \(\mathbf Q\). These sixteen checks
are additional computations; the displayed resolution proves
the interpolation statement for every \(r\).

## 2. Finite normal restriction as an exact morphism

Fix a pair \(e\), use the stabilizer splitting \(E=P_e\oplus W_e\),
and set \(r=s-1\). The complement of \(\mathbf P(W_e)\) in
\(\mathbf P(E)\) is the total space of
\(W_e\otimes\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(P_e)}(1)\).
The image \(\mathcal B^r_{e,k}(c)\) of the ideal sheaf in the
order-\(r\) normal quotient is, as a module on the base line,
\[
\bigoplus_{0\le j<r}
\operatorname{Sym}^jW_e^*
\otimes (XY)^{k-j}\mathcal O(c-j-2(k-j)).
\tag{SD1}
\]
The exponent \(k-j\) is exactly the remaining endpoint
Taylor order. The other three frame points lie off this line
and impose no condition on its finite normal sheaf.

For precision, define a finite morphism of truncated normal
neighborhoods
\[
t:\operatorname{Tot}_{<r}(W_e\otimes\mathcal O(-1))
\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Tot}_{<r}(W_e\otimes\mathcal O(1)),
\qquad w=XYv.
\tag{SD2}
\]
The notation means that all monomials of normal degree at
least \(r\) have been set to zero. The map is finite because
both structure algebras are finite over the base line.
The coefficient map
\[
F\longmapsto (XY)^{-k}F(X,Y,XYv)
\]
defines an isomorphism
\[
\mathcal B^r_{e,k}(c)\simeq t_*\mathcal O(-s)
\tag{SD3}
\]
of modules for the original normal-neighborhood algebra.
Indeed each normal degree \(j\) in (SD1) contains
\((XY)^{k-j}\); substitution contributes \((XY)^j\),
and cancellation leaves an ordinary regular coefficient.
The inverse multiplies that coefficient by
\((XY)^{k-j}\). The original normal coordinate acts on the
right side by \(XYv\). This proves (SD3) at the endpoints
without inverting \(X\) or \(Y\) in their local rings.

The projection formula consequently gives the actual comparison
\[
\mathcal B^r_{e,k}(c)\otimes S_{(a,b)}Q
\simeq
t_*\bigl(\mathcal O(-s)\otimes S_{(a,b)}t^*Q\bigr).
\tag{SD4}
\]
This identifies exactly the bundle to which the report's
unipotent automorphism is applied.

Write \(p=X\ell_i+Y\ell_j\). On the source of (SD2), put
\[
T=I-\frac12\bigl((Yv)\otimes X^*+(Xv)\otimes Y^*\bigr).
\]
The products \(Xv,Yv\) are global regular \(W_e\)-valued
functions: their two homogeneous degrees cancel. Its
correction has square zero, since both coordinate
functionals vanish on \(W_e\). Thus \(T\) is invertible
with the displayed sign-reversed inverse, and
\[
T(p+XYv)=p.
\]
It is symmetric under endpoint interchange and equivariant
under the other three letters. The induced actual quotient
bundle isomorphism is
\[
t^*Q\simeq
(\det P_e)\mathcal O(1)\oplus W_e.
\tag{SD5}
\]
Equations (SD2)–(SD5) verify all normal couplings, including
the original linear-form differential.

## 3. The global cohomology comparison

For both twists \(C=c\) and \(C=c-1\), the report's binary
overlap functionals compare the coefficients of exponents
\(t\) and \(C-j-t\), with
\[
C-k+1\le t\le k-j-1.
\]
For a normal monomial of degree \(j<r\), its point Taylor
degree is \(t+j\). In the source it is at least \(k-s\),
which is at least \(2s-1\) in the stated range and hence
at least \(2r\). At each fixed total Taylor degree the
leading functionals are exactly a subset of the directional
jets from §1. Chart changes are triangular in the total
degree, with invertible leading coordinate changes.
Taking a largest degree in a proposed relation and descending
therefore proves that every overlap coefficient vanishes.
This proves surjectivity of both scalar restriction maps.

The target dimension is established by the already verified
Cox grading from A-028. Its six binary weights are
\((k-s)^5,k-3s\). For \(k\ge3s\), the binary weight difference is
\[
[z^{2k-s}]
\frac{(1-z^{k-s+1})^5}{(1-z)^4}
=
\binom{2k-s+3}{3}
-5\binom{k+2}{3}
+10\binom{s+1}{3}.
\]
Terms of numerator order at least three have negative
residual degree. At \(k=3s-1\), the sixth binary weight is
\(-1\); the component is zero. The displayed coefficient
also vanishes by the equality of binary weights \(-1\)
and \(1\), or by direct substitution into the binomial
expression. Hence the endpoint has the same formula.

Subtracting the fat-point length proves
\[
h^1(I^k(c))=10\binom{s+1}{3}.
\]
Each normal image has first-cohomology dimension
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{s-2}(j+1)(s-j-1)=\binom{s+1}{3}.
\]
The target scalar restriction is therefore an isomorphism
and the preceding source restriction is onto. The two
maps form the commuting diagram with the actual
locally split Schur complex. Its scalar twists have no
\(H^2,H^3\), so the cokernel on first cohomology gives
the full Schur-bundle first cohomology, and all groups
of degree at least two vanish. This verifies the
global-to-finite-normal comparison in full.

## 4. The exact summands and positive count

Applying the one-line branching maps to (SD5) removes a
horizontal strip of row lengths \(u,v\), with
\(0\le u\le x\), \(0\le v\le b\). Combining these maps
with (SD4) and the line Čech pairing gives
\[
\bigoplus_{\substack{j,u,v\ge0\\u\le x,\ v\le b\\j+u+v\le s-2}}
(\det P_e)^{u+v+1}
\operatorname{Sym}^{s-j-u-v-2}P_e
\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^jW_e^*
\otimes S_{(b+x-u,b-v)}W_e.
\tag{SD6}
\]
The factor \(\det P_e\) comes from
\(H^1(\mathcal O(-m))=\operatorname{Sym}^{m-2}P_e\otimes\det P_e\).
The ten pairs are transitively permuted, so their sum
is exactly induction from \(S_2\times S_3\).

The nine-variable inequalities D.17 were checked against

\[
2z_2+3z_3=j+x-u+v-2h-e
\]
counts precisely the three possible symmetric-power
multiplicity series on the two-dimensional standard
representation. The fixed horizontal/vertical strip

Each parity slack is uniquely determined and nonnegative
when its parity is correct, so it introduces no

### The normal-order map and Cauchy extraction

Put \(r=m-2\). The degree-\(N\) Cauchy decomposition of
\(\operatorname{Sym}(E\otimes F)\) contains precisely the
partitions with at most \(r\) rows. The quotient
\(E\to Q\) gives an actual map
\(S_\alpha E\to H^0(S_\alpha Q)\).
The primitive-idempotent image of
\([\mathcal O(-1)\to E]^{\otimes N}\), with its Koszul
signs, has degree-\(j\) terms indexed by vertical
\(j\)-strips. Thus \(j\le r\). Every negative line
twist \(\mathcal O(-j)\), \(1\le j\le r\), is acyclic
on \(\mathbf P^r\). The locally split tensor
contraction proves exactness before taking sections,
so the quotient map itself induces the asserted
section isomorphism.

At the frame point represented by \(e_0=\ell_i\),
the moving quotient sends
\[
e_0\longmapsto-\sum_jx_je_j.
\]
Its induced algebra map is exactly
\[
Y_{0a}\longmapsto-\sum_jx_jY_{ja}.
\tag{FR1}
\]
Over the fraction field in the remaining rows, the
\(r\times r\) matrix \(Y=(Y_{ja})\) is invertible.
Consequently the least nonzero homogeneous degree
in the \(Y_0\) variables survives (FR1) as exactly
the same \(x\)-degree. Later homogeneous pieces have
larger degree and cannot cancel it. The polynomial
coefficients in the other rows encode the entire
Schur component faithfully. Therefore membership in
\(I_i^k\) is equivalent to order-\(k\) vanishing
of the section, and intersection over all frame
points gives the actual isomorphism FA.2. This
checks the order, rather than merely the value at
the point.

### Product, saturation and the signed complex

At a homogeneous prime different from the irrelevant
ideal, at most \(m-2\) of the \(I_i\) are contained
in that prime: any \(m-1\) frame vectors span \(E\).
Their independent vectors can be completed to a
basis, making their ideals disjoint variable blocks.
Every other ideal is a unit at the prime. For
disjoint blocks, membership in all \(k\)-th powers
is equivalent to degree at least \(k\) in every
block, which is exactly product membership.
Thus the product and intersection have the same
ideal sheaf.

Each block power is saturated: a complementary
variable does not change membership, so a class
killed by an irrelevant-ideal power is already
zero. Intersections preserve saturation. This
proves that the saturation of \(P_k\) is \(J_k\).
Conca–Herzog applies to the \(mk\) repeated nonzero
linear ideals, giving regularity \(mk\) and saturation
degree at most \(mk\). Hence FA.3 and the required
higher-cohomology vanishing hold in the exact
stated range.

The differential in the restriction complex adds
one index with its ordered-subset sign. A frame
permutation has the sign of reordering the image
subset. This is its actual equivariant orientation
line. On a disjoint-block chart, a monomial survives
in the term for \(A\) precisely when every index
in \(A\) belongs to the set of block powers that
do not contain that monomial. Its augmented complex
is the full simplex on that set, contracted by
inserting its least index. This proves sheaf
exactness with the specified maps.

For a subset of size \(s\le m-2\), the quotient
is free over the polynomial ring in the complementary
variables, with normal-monomial shifts at most
\(s(k-1)\). At \(N\ge mk\), all residual twists are
nonnegative; higher cohomology vanishes and global
sections equal the indicated graded pieces. For
\(s\ge m-1\), already \(m-1\) independent truncated
blocks have maximum degree \((m-1)(k-1)<mk\);
their degree-\(N\) component and sheaf vanish.
Regularity also makes the union sheaf acyclic
in these twists and its sections equal to
\(S_N/(J_k)_N\). These observations prove that
taking global sections gives exactly FA.4,
including its last term and all endpoints.

### Stabilizers, flags and characters

For a subset \(A\), the explicit complement \(W_A\)
consists of the zero-sum vectors supported on the
other letters. If
\(\sum_{i\in A}c_i\ell_i\in W_A\), its coordinates

\]

\otimes\operatorname{Sym}(\mathfrak h_{m-|A|}\otimes F).

The subgroup on \(A\) permutes the first tensor

The full exterior-column pairing gives

The line twist cancels against

### The coherent and locally free \(K_0\) maps

The revised dictionary paragraph is valid.
For completeness, its equivariant resolution
construction terminates by the following direct
argument. At each syzygy \(M_i\), choose an invariant
graded lift of \(M_i/S_+M_i\). Each such space is
finite dimensional, and reductivity of
\(S_m\times GL(F)\) over \(\mathbf Q\) supplies
the lift. The resulting maps
\(S\otimes W_i\to M_i\) are surjective by graded
Nakayama. Their kernels are finitely generated
because \(S\) is Noetherian. This constructs a
minimal equivariant graded free resolution.

If \(D=\dim(E\otimes F)\), the variable Koszul
complex resolves \(\mathbf Q\) in \(D\) steps.
Its exactness follows successively because each
variable is a nonzero divisor modulo its predecessors.
It computes \(\operatorname{Tor}_i^S(M,\mathbf Q)\),
which is zero for \(i>D\). The minimal resolution
has zero differentials after tensoring with
\(\mathbf Q\), so
\[
F_i/S_+F_i=\operatorname{Tor}_i^S(M,\mathbf Q)=0
\quad(i>D).
\]
Graded Nakayama gives \(F_i=0\). Thus the displayed
equivariant resolution is finite, with actual maps.

Sheafification sends each free term to a locally
free equivariant sheaf, and alternating sum gives
its exact \(K_0\) class. Comparison lifts between
resolutions are equivariant because
\(\operatorname{Hom}_{S,G}(S\otimes W,-)\)
is exact; their acyclic mapping cones have zero
alternating class. The same construction on a
short exact sequence gives additivity. This
proves the stated coherent-to-locally-free map,
with its independence of choices.

## A-051. The complete all-degree quotient theorem T049

**Result: complete proof PASS.** The entire report
work/theta/fat_arrangement_product_report.md,
DP.1–DP.12, was read. It proves the exact
all-degree equality for \(1\le r\le m-2\).

In the independent-block ring \(R\), the ideal
\(D=\prod_i\mathfrak a_i^k\) equals the intersection
by literal block degrees. The oriented subset
restriction complex resolves \(R/D\); its monomial
components have the same explicit simplex
contraction checked above. For a proper subset,
an unselected block can be replaced by the
diagonal variables \(L_a=\sum_iY_{ia}\).
This gives \(R_A=B_A[L_1,\ldots,L_r]\)
with the selected-block relations unchanged.
Thus the Koszul homology in positive degree
vanishes on every proper-subset term.

In the bounded Koszul–restriction bicomplex,
a subset of size \(s\) has cohomological degree
\(q=s-1\), and Koszul degree \(i\) contributes
\(-i\). Proper subsets survive only at \(i=0\),
so \(q-i\ge0\). The full subset has
\(q-i\ge m-1-r\ge1\). No spectral-sequence
entry has negative total degree. Hence the
negative total cohomology vanishes, giving
\[
\operatorname{Tor}_{i>0}^R(R/D,R/(L))=0.
\]
The ideal sequence gives the literal injection
\(D/LD\to R/(L)\) with image \(P_k\), as well
as all positive Tor vanishing for \(D\).
This is the asserted quotient morphism.

The ordered sequence is regular on \(D\):
the last-form mapping-cone sequence makes that
form surjective on the positive Koszul homology
of the preceding sequence. These finitely
generated graded modules are bounded below,
so graded Nakayama makes them zero. Induction
and the same sequence prove the required
injectivity at degree zero.

For each block ideal, \(H^0\) of local cohomology
is zero. Its block Čech complex has no cohomology
below degree one. Tensoring these complexes
over \(\mathbf Q\) gives the full-variable Čech
complex on \(D\); the vector-space Künneth formula
therefore gives \(H^j_{R_+}(D)=0\) for \(j<m\).
Quotienting successively by the regular diagonal
sequence yields
\[
H^j_{S_+}(P_k)=0\quad(j<m-r).

## 1. Tensor pairings and the actual incidence map

The nested symmetric pairing is the restriction of the ordinary

therefore the adjoint of averaging inclusion. The averaging

inverse as adjoint. These facts prove the exact transpose identity
\[
h_{d,e}(V)^*=h_{e,d}(V^*)
\]
with scalar one. In particular, each subsequent use of transpose
identifies the rank of the particular map being studied.

For the multilinear block basis \(q_L\) of

inclusion gives coefficient \(1/[v!(u!)^v]\) to every ordered
row arrangement. A transverse unordered column partition has
exactly \(v!u!\) such arrangements: choose the order of its rows
and columns, after which each cell is prescribed by the unique
intersection element. Hence its coefficient is
\[
(u!)^{1-v}.
\]
A nontransverse column partition cannot arise. Thus the incidence
matrix is related to the normalized canonical map by the exact
formula OF.8, and in the fourth square the scalar is \(24^{-3}\).

The passage to every dimension retains these same multiplicity

## 1. Validity, grading and the canonical point-jet map

The partition inequality is exactly \(2b+x+k\ge6\).
Its size is \(5(d+b+x+k-2)\), its second-row excess over

\[

\]
Thus \(N=|\alpha|\ge5k\) is precisely the same validity
inequality. The determinant identity for \(Q\), of rank three,
gives \(S_\alpha Q=\mathcal O(c)S_{(a,b)}Q\), since
\((\det E)^c\) is trivial for even \(c\). The actual chart map
then gives exactly the sign \(\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}\).

The bundle \(S_{(a,b)}Q\) is generated by the quotient of
\(S_{(a,b)}E\). At a fixed point, select global sections spanning
its fiber. Every homogeneous tangent monomial of degree \(j<k\)
is the leading jet of a scalar degree-\(c\) section that vanishes
to order \(j\), because \(c\ge k-1\). Multiplication by the
selected bundle sections spans the entire degree-\(j\) jet
quotient. Correcting jets in increasing order changes none of
the already prescribed lower degrees. This proves surjectivity
onto the full one-point jet space.

The map itself is the canonical restriction map. G-027's
least-normal-degree substitution identifies its kernel with
the indicated \(I_i^k\) Schur component. Hence the singleton
term is canonically the full direct sum of point jets, with its
literal frame-permutation action. No simultaneous independent
prescription at all five points is asserted by this one-point
argument; the subsequent exact complex computes precisely its
global cokernel.

## 2. The pair term and its actual maps

At subset size three, the complementary space has dimension one.

truncated tensor factors would need to supply at least
\[

\]

term is zero. The larger subset terms vanish in degree \(N\ge5k\)
as already proved in G-027.

At size two, the complementary factor has at most two rows.
It must omit the third row of \(\alpha\), of length
\(c=2(k-1)\). This already uses the entire maximum degree of
the two truncated factors. Thus their degrees are each \(k-1\);
the complementary partition is exactly \((a+c,b+c)\);
and the removed skew shape is a single horizontal row of
length \(c\). Its only Schur type is \((c)\).

The multiplication map
\[

\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^{c}F
\]
therefore induces an isomorphism on the required component.
Its restriction to that unique top summand is nonzero, as seen
on a pure power; normalized symmetric comultiplication supplies

fixes multiplication, so no extra pair sign occurs here.

Multiplication of the Cauchy copy in rows \(z_1,z_2\) by
\(\det(v,z_1,z_2)^c\) is injective in the polynomial domain.
Its \(F\)-type is \(S_\alpha F\), and its \(W\)-type is

multiplicity space. Since \(c\) is even, its determinant
character on \(S_3\) is trivial. The ordered-subset orientation
is exactly \(\operatorname{sgn}_{S_2}\).
Induction over the ten pairs gives the module in ER.2.

## 4. Traces and polynomial bounds

The signed tensor Schur complex gives the three scalar Euler
terms in ER.9, with the omitted-partition endpoints encoded by

## 2. Seeds, monoid and a rigorous closure argument

For the three positive gaps write
\((a,b,c)=(1,1,1)+p+2t\).
The original \(t\) satisfies the required congruence, so a minimal
admissible \(u\le t\) exists. A total of at least five contains
a nonempty zero-sum subvector: list five indexed residues and
use equality of two of their six partial sums modulo five.
Removing it contradicts minimality. The total-at-most-four
enumeration therefore includes every minimal seed.

The same partial-sum argument shows that every indecomposable
nonzero increment has total at most five. A longer element
contains a proper zero-sum subvector of length at most five.
Recursive subtraction thus expresses every increment in terms
of the eight independently enumerated generators.
Every such increment has the actual G-024 invariant-section
embedding. Full positivity is therefore preserved by every
further monoid increment.

The graph is best interpreted as a set of actual inputs:
an unstable node represents one point, and a stable node
represents its whole nonnegative first-axis progression of
step ten. Every deficient seed belongs to this represented set.
For an unstable node, each stored edge directly places its
successor in that set or in the upward-closed full-support set.

For a stable point \(g+10q(1,0,0)\), adding a generator gives
\[
(g+2h)+10q(1,0,0).
\]
The multiplier for \(h\) and the first-axis multiplier commute
as elements of the same polynomial algebra. First use the stored
edge for \(g+2h\). If it is a full-support exit, all further
axis increments preserve full support. Otherwise retain its
normal representative and any actual stable offset already
removed. Apply the recorded first-axis edge successively for
the remaining finite number of increments. While the state is
unstable, this increases its first gap until it either exits or
reaches the new threshold. At a stable state, the further
increments are isomorphisms and its first-axis edge is a loop
in the represented set.

This explicitly treats an increment that raises \(b,c\) and
raises the stability threshold. It never assumes that the
normal form commutes with that increment. Induction on a finite
generator expression proves that every deficient input is
represented by a listed point or ray. Conversely every listed
point has a deficient computed module, and every represented
stable point has that same module by the actual isomorphism.
This proves both directions of the classification.

## 1. Validity, jet maps and cohomology

Write \(a=b+x\), \(c=2k-3\), and

S_\alpha Q=(\det E)^c\mathcal O(c)S_{(a,b)}Q
=\operatorname{sgn}_5\mathcal O(c)S_{(a,b)}Q.
\]
The chart sign is therefore \(\operatorname{sgn}^{d+a}\),
as stated, since \(\lambda_2=d+a+c\) and \(c\) is odd.

Because \(c\ge k-1\), every scalar homogeneous tangent jet
of order less than \(k\) occurs as the leading jet of a section
of \(\mathcal O(c)\). Global sections of \(S_{(a,b)}Q\)
generate its fiber. Multiplying these sections and correcting
jets successively gives the canonical surjection onto each full
point-jet module. This is the individual point map; its direct
sum has exactly the cokernel computed by the arrangement complex.
G-027's normal-order substitution identifies its kernel with the
displayed Schur component of the point ideal power.

The ambient bundle is acyclic, and a finite point-jet sheaf has
no positive cohomology. Thus its restriction cokernel is precisely
\(H^1\) of the ideal-twisted bundle, with every higher group
zero. The exact degree-\(|\alpha|\) arrangement complex now
identifies this cokernel with the kernel of the actual signed
quotient \(K_2\to K_3\). Its later terms vanish in the proved
degree range. This establishes ET.4 with the stated maps, not

## 1. Exact map and kernel membership

The averaged tensor evaluation pairing gives
\(h_{b,a}^*=h_{a,b}\) on the dual space, with scalar one.
Consequently the actual image annihilator is the displayed lower
canonical kernel; its Schur multiplicity equals the cokernel
multiplicity being bounded. This is the same exact pairing already
fully audited in A-053, and its use in FK.4 has the correct indices.

The normalized outer comultiplication \(\delta\) has
multiplication as a left inverse. For \(r+1\) outer slots,
the common coefficient extraction then gives exactly
\[
\Theta F(v_1,\ldots,v_r;x,y)=
\binom br^r\mathcal A_F
(x^rv_1^{b-r},\ldots,x^rv_r^{b-r},y^b).
\]
There is no unspecified scalar in this formula.

The lower-kernel membership proof was reread in full in R-024
P.9–P.16. A split form \((x^r+c y^r)Q\) is a product of
\(b\) linear forms over \(\mathbf C\). Its first coefficient
in \(c\) gives the vanishing with last argument \(y^rQ\).
Applying the \(b-r\) directional derivatives corresponding
to the factors of \(Q\) to the last argument \(y^b\)
gives exactly the scalar \(b!/r!\) times this vanishing.
Before derivative \(i\), the exchanged variables have degrees
\(b-i+1\) and \(r\), with positive difference
\(b-r-i+1\). On a two-letter string
\(\det^j\operatorname{Sym}^{p+q-2j}\), the derivative
has nonzero coefficient \(p-j\), since \(j\le q<p\).
It is therefore injective on the full bidegree and on every
multiplicity space. The other variables are spectators. Removing
the derivatives successively proves the required vanishing with
last argument \(y^b\). Evaluation in \(x,y\) separates
the two exterior symmetric factors, so the image lies in the
tensor product with the actual lower canonical kernel.

All maps and coefficients are rational; proving the polynomial
identities over \(\mathbf C\) proves their rational identities.
Extension to every characteristic-zero field preserves the kernels
and the injectivity of the resulting linear maps.

## 2. Full-multiplicity injection and its iteration

For \(b_{r+1}=C_{r+1}+t\), the exact recurrence gives
\(b_{r+1}-r=b_r\ge t\ge1\). After \(\delta\),
every first-factor type \(\nu\) contributing to a
\(\lambda\)-type is contained in \(\lambda\), by the
horizontal-strip Pieri rule. Thus \(\nu_2\le t\le b_r\).

The full R-018 proof was reread: every highest polynomial is a
linear combination of products of flag minors; after separate
dehomogenization, each slot block has degree at most
\(\nu_2\). At common vector \(e_1\), the coefficient map

\(\prod_i\binom{b-d_i}{r}\). Every factor is nonzero in
the stated range. Division by these exact factors gives an inverse
on the polynomial subspace. The equivariant kernel therefore has
no highest vector of the indicated type, proving injectivity on
the entire isotypic space rather than on a selected vector.

The direct sum of these first-factor types is still injective:
distinct isotypic images remain distinct before tensoring by the
last symmetric factor. Tensoring preserves injectivity. In the
resulting codomain every lower kernel type is contained in the
output type by two applications of Pieri, and hence has second
row at most \(t\). This proves exactly FK.9.

Iterating this specified map on its middle factor, using ordinary
factor permutations, gives FK.10. The degree identity
\((r+1)b_{r+1}-r b_r=r^2+b_{r+1}\) checks at every stage.
No projection onto an unspecified image or multiplicity basis is
needed in this iteration.

## 3. Complete finite tails and exact exclusions

The independent script `check_finite_base_tails_independent.py`

# Primary oscillator source audit

Statement **A-059**. Checked 21 November 2026 by GPT-6 Astra Pro,
run `/root/archive_audit`; effort setting not exposed.

Primary source: T. Basile, E. Joung, K. Mkrtchyan and M. Mojaza,
*Dual Pair Correspondence in Physics: Oscillator Realizations and
Representations*, arXiv:2006.07102v2, subsequently JHEP 09 (2020) 020,
DOI 10.1007/JHEP09(2020)020.
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.07102v2

The web PDF fetch returned a disabled-fetch error. A direct request
to that same primary URL then returned an actual 952017-byte PDF,
saved as `OSCILLATOR_DUALITY_2020V2.pdf`; extracted text is saved
alongside. This audit read the text and mathematical formulas,
without claiming new visual inspection of the page images.

## Exact passages read

- §5.1, (5.7)–(5.20), printed pp.28–29: compact oscillator
  realization, central shifts, Young conditions and Cauchy duality.
- Entire §5.2, (5.21)–(5.30), printed pp.29–31: the
  \(U(M_+,M_-)\), \(U(N)\) differential operators, minimal
  oscillator state, contraction conditions and mixed highest weight.
- Appendix A, (A.21)–(A.28), printed pp.76–77, together with
  the surrounding derivation: the mixed tensor, exterior-column
  contraction and the resulting complementary highest weight.
- The representation convention (1.16), printed p.7; the
  explicit cover discussion (2.12)–(2.18), printed p.10; and
  (2.23)–(2.25), printed p.11. These specify the source's use
  of double-cover compact groups and its half-integral weights.

## Statements established by these passages

The differential operators in (5.21) have diagonal shifts
\(+N/2\) in the positive block and \(-N/2\) in the
negative block. The compact partner (5.22) has scalar diagonal
shift \((M_+-M_-)/2\). The contraction equations (5.28)
identify the mixed traceless tensor of (5.29), whose unshifted
highest weight is
\[
(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_p,0,\ldots,0,-m_q,\ldots,-m_1).
\]
The exterior-column Levi–Civita contraction in (A.25) is the
actual map to the polynomial highest weight obtained after a
determinant twist; (A.26)–(A.28) display that weight explicitly.
The strict range \(p+q<N\) proposed for T-052 lies within
all the dimensional inequalities used in this passage.

The source explicitly includes the covering-group convention.
Its symbols must retain that convention when the displayed
half-integral generators are used literally. For example a
positive-block vacuum coordinate of weight \(N/2\) acquires
\((-1)^N\) around the corresponding \(2\pi\) circle. This
is an exact monodromy calculation, and (2.12)–(2.18) explains
the analogous issue in the source. A proposed unshifted action
or an honest-group identification needs its actual changed
generators and integration, rather than suppressing the shifts.
No objection to the source's stated cover convention is claimed.

## A precise equality-boundary correction

The sentence immediately before (A.23), printed p.76, says that
traceless tensors vanish at \(p+q\ge N\). At equality this
is false. For \(N=2\), let \(e_1,e_2\) be the standard
basis and \(e_1^*,e_2^*\) its dual. The actual contraction
\[
\mathbf C^2\otimes(\mathbf C^2)^*\longrightarrow\mathbf C,
\qquad v\otimes\phi\longmapsto\phi(v)
\]
kills the nonzero tensor \(e_1\otimes e_2^*\). It has
the two one-box symmetries, so \(p=q=1\) and \(p+q=N\).
It is the highest vector of weight \((1,-1)\) for the usual
upper-triangular convention. Thus the equality claim is refuted
by the displayed morphism. The source's later paragraph before
(A.28) correctly permits \(p+q\le N\), as does (A.21).
The intended T-052 range is strict and does not use the rejected
equality sentence.

This is a source audit and an explicit boundary correction. It
does not certify the entire new T-052 construction, which had
not yet been supplied when these checks were recorded.

For \(e=0\), summation gives

## 2. Operators, adjoints and real dual pair

The Weyl relations give exactly
\[
[C_a,R_b]=\sum_iX_{bi}\partial_{X_{ai}}
+\delta_{ab}(N_Y+m)=A_{ba}-\delta_{ab}A_{00}.
\]
Together with the compact brackets this verifies every block

Their commutators with \(R_a\) cancel literally, as do
their derivative commutators with \(C_a\). The common center
has exactly the scalar \(m(r-1)/2\), and every \(A\)
preserves each individual charge.

The factorial monomial form gives \(R_a^\dagger=C_a\)

the two mixed matrix coefficients are complex conjugates,
while the represented operators are negative adjoints.
This gives the asserted skew-adjoint real action. The compact
real form follows from \(B_{ij}^\dagger=B_{ji}\).

A real-linear commutant of \(U(r,1)\) commutes with its

unitaries and a mixed boost span the matrix units on
\(H=\mathbf C^{r,1}\), so its complex commutant on
\(H\otimes W\) is \(1\otimes\operatorname{End}W\).
Preserving the imaginary Hermitian form and complex linearity
recovers its real part, giving exactly \(U(m)\). The reverse
centralizer is obtained by the same calculation.

The positive compatible complex structure is \(i\) on the
positive part and \(-i\) on the negative part. The latter
turns its creation representation into \(W^*\), giving

\[
(\det a)^m z^{-m}(\det g)^{r-1}.
\]
The vacuum square and its half derivatives therefore give
every shift in OC.7, including the negative-block sign.

The source cover convention was checked in A-059, and this

A block-homogeneous monomial of degree \(d_i\ge k\) has

On the finite charge-degree space, the denominator's

The rightmost derivative in

## 4. Harmonic irreducibles and all dual maps

Cauchy extraction gives a row type \(S_\alpha F\) and the

of a relation, and each reduction preserves the ideal residue.
The standard monomials are therefore a basis. Because every
step also lowers the displayed monomial order, the initial ideal
is exactly \((M_1,\ldots,M_r)\).

For a nonzero standard representative modulo the first \(a-1\)
relations, the leading monomial of \(R_af\) is
\(M_a\operatorname{in}(f)\). Its new factors are disjoint
from the previous leading monomials, so it remains indivisible
by them and cannot disappear under reduction. This proves each
required nonzerodivisor step, hence the regular sequence.

The same diamond proof works over \(\mathbf Q[s]\),
with rule \(M_a\mapsto sT_a\); both two-rule paths give
\(s^2T_aT_b\). Thus the standard monomials form a free
\(\mathbf Q[s]\)-basis and the family is flat.
The general-fiber map sends the family diagonal coordinate
to \(sX_{aa}\), fixes the other variables, and carries its
relation to \(sR_a\). The inverse uses \(s^{-1}X_{aa}\).
Both preserve all stated torus gradings. Selecting equal
nonnegative charge pieces is a direct sum of free graded
pieces, hence gives the asserted flat Rees family.

## 3. Literal bounded polytopes and smaller-row transport

A standard monomial has exponents \(u_{ai},v_i\).
Its row weights and charge are precisely
\[
\sum_i u_{ai}=\eta_a,\qquad \sum_a u_{ai}-v_i=k.
\]
It avoids \(X_{aa}Y_a\) exactly when \(u_{aa}=0\) or
\(v_a=0\). The unique tag
\(A=\{a\le r:v_a>0\}\) consequently gives all constraints
in IR.8 and their inverse monomial map. There is no duplicate
at \(u_{aa}=v_a=0\), because that index belongs to the
complementary tag. Row sums bound every \(u\), and the column
equations bound every \(v\), so all these polytopes are bounded.
The impossible total degree and the zero-weight constant
endpoints follow immediately by summing the equations.

When \(r<m-2\), padding the row highest weight by zeros
is an actual inclusion of polynomial spaces. The new zero row
degrees force independence from the new variables; the new
compact raising and lowering equations vanish. Thus the highest
multiplicity spaces are literally identified.

The added inverse labels are correct. With
\(\gamma=(\alpha,0^{m-r-1},-b)\), \(t=\alpha_1\),
\(n=t-k\), and
\(\lambda=t\mathbf1-\operatorname{reverse}\gamma\),
one has \(t\ge N/r\ge k\), \(|\lambda|=m(t-k)\),
and \(\lambda_2=t\). This is a nonnegative partition,
including the stated empty case. The exact T-052 column pairing
and finite Gram dual map give the outer transpose at odd \(t\).
Consequently IR.10 identifies every multiplicity, every Kostka
weight and every Specht dimension in the positive weighted sum.
The whole row-weight count is exactly that sum.

## 4. Exact finite-group obstruction

The degree-two ideal is the \(r\)-dimensional span of the
\(R_a\)'s. Their supports consist only of \(X_{ai}Y_i\).
For any monomial order, the degree-two initial space has the
same dimension and all its monomials belong to this set.
This remains true for an order that is not degree-compatible:
the ideal is homogeneous, and a degree-two leading monomial
comes from its degree-two homogeneous component. No relation
exists in smaller degree.

The literal column-permutation orbit of \(X_{ai}Y_i\)
has exactly the \(m\) distinct monomials \(X_{aj}Y_j\).
A stable monomial subspace containing one would contain them
all. Since \(1\le r\le m-2\), its dimension \(r\) makes
that impossible. This proves IR.11 for the stated action and
coordinates. It does not assert a failure for other coordinate
systems or other constructions; the original quotient keeps
the exact permutation action supplied by the algebra map.

## 5. Equivariant resolution and geometric transport

The proved regular sequence gives the written Koszul resolution.
The relation span transforms as \(F\), so its exterior factors
are \(\Lambda^jF\), with bidegree shift \((j,j)\).
The actual differential is multiplication by \(R_{a_h}\)
with its exterior deletion sign. The compact \(GL(W)\)
fixes every \(R_a\), and each has charge zero. These facts
prove the full equivariance and the exact charge extraction.

The selected weight and bidegree spaces are exact direct summands
for the rational torus action. Taking their Euler classes gives
IR.14 with the correct row exterior factors and degrees.
The first equality is T-052's actual rational harmonic projector.
Under homogenization, its cyclic tensor trace agrees with the
factored T-049 truncated character.

The free resolution is used on \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal P\)
or after exact graded sheafification on
\(\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal P\). The report does not
assert preservation of that resolution by a nonflat pullback
to a different Proj. The Rees comparison is a separate actual
graded algebra isomorphism, hence identifies its own affine
scheme and relative Proj charts. Every geometric base and
every map in this transport is therefore specified.

The arbitrary-power R-018 inverse uses the factors
